matches.note: I-quit (submission) match: “The Supreme Master of Controversy” Adam Finn (Hybrid) beat “The Definer of Hardcore” Chomps, who submitted to the Ankle Lock (14:45). Finn then unmasked as the Great Jita and turned on Jaxx before their Intercontinental title match (matches[4]).

Tag team match for the World Tag Team titles, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Street Science, Studog Escobar and E Razor, beat the champions the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores (CHL#2 and CHL#3, unnamed in the text) when Studog Escobar pinned CHL#3 after the Nuclear Mega-Ton Escobomb (19:02).

date.source: GIWF title-history ledger (World Title change dated to this PPV)

matches.stipulation: Tag-Title Match - Venetian Home Rumble II

matches.note: Triangle match refereed by Uriah Rennie: the champion Luca, in the L.U.C.A.B.O.T., retained the North American title against “The Supreme Master of Controversy” Hybrid and Enigma, who submitted to the Pneumatic Nut Crush (25:54). Luca’s makeshift Bullabot fell apart early; Benito Cavalera and Snake Phoenix brought him a repaired LUCABOT in return for joining them, and Max Damage laid him out with a chair. During the match Jay Phoenix walked to the timekeeper’s table and carried the North American title belt up the ramp.

Four corners match for the World title with The Prodigy as special guest referee: the champion “The Stylemeister” Lyle Wile, “The Corporal” Cpl. Punishment, “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) and “The Bastard” Al Crud. As Al Crud covered Cpl. Punishment, Lew Spectre came back in to break up the pin and grabbed Cpl. Punishment’s ankle; the Prodigy counted three and Al Crud won the World title for the third time (28:10).

Tag match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Team Esco (Henrique Escobar and John Barnes) beat Pretty in the City (Daneel and Mark McCord; the team and Mark McCord have no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when John Barnes’ Time Warp made Mark McCord submit (7:30).

For the GIWF North American Tag-Team Titles: the Phenomenal Pets (Montezuma the camel and Borrico Agujero’s pet) hung above the ring in a cage; the first man to climb the ladder, reach the remote and lower the cage won the pets and the titles. Shane Stone retrieved the remote and the Phenomenons won the titles from Tropical Storm (12:23).

Main event for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, refereed by Uriah Rennie, under the elimination rules Commissioner Childress (Nephilim) imposed: Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn), Cpl. Punishment and Ace Thunder, who came out despite the Youngbloods’ attack on his knee that afternoon. Ace Thunder eliminated the Corporal with the Thunderclap; Spectre made Ace Thunder submit to the Figure-Four Sleeper (15:29) and won the World title.

For the GIWF World Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Forces of Darkness (Jared Crafter and Riggs) against the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores, led to the ring by CHL #1, who had taken the belts from them on Wednesday Night Global. CHL #3 pinned Riggs after a spear (15:56).

matches.stipulation: Last Man Standing/Falls Count Anywhere/Anything Goes

matches.note: For the GIWF Television Title, refereed by Des Galpin: the champion Lee Coulter against a mystery opponent. The commentary announced Shane Stone; instead the RPA came out and revealed Trent Lucas, walking again after his injuries. Trent Lucas pinned Coulter with the Spotlight (13:52) and became the new Television Champion.

For the GIWF Intercontinental Title, refereed by Isiah Heywood: Jay Phoenix (champion) was billed against Evil of the Dark Lords, but Evil never came out — Luca revealed the booking as a ruse and brought out a rebuilt LUCABOT. Luca in LUCABOT made Jay Phoenix submit to the Pneumatic Nut Crush (12:45) and became Intercontinental Champion, completing the GIWF Grand Slam. Later that night Jay Phoenix accompanied Celest in the World Title main event and hit Corporal Punishment with a springboard moonsault.

name: Fear the Raine

matches.stipulation: Barbed Wire Thumbtack Baseball Bat match

matches.note: The GIWF Intercontinental Championship changed hands: Cockney Rebel went after Shane Stone as he taunted him from the ramp and Neil Scott counted the pin in nine seconds. The Youngbloods’ masked assault followed (Stone introducing Eric Cameron as his new tag partner) and Stone was left handcuffed to the ropes.

eliminations.note: counted out with Akira after Cage (the IWF’s rival North American claimant) drew him under the ring

matches.note: For the GIWF North American Championship. Both falls ended in double countouts — Spectre and Akira, then Pete Steele and the Bum Boozler (the Boozler and Gimp beating Steele down) — and Steele kept the title.
For the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship: Hamish McGrubber won the title when Curt Raines could not answer the ten count (20:13).

notes: Unlisted bout: Billed as The Guv’nor v. Richard Ray Vaughn, a managers’ hardcore challenge; the man in the ring was Lew Spectre in a silicone Vaughn mask, and the “Spectre” at ringside was Vaughn. The Guv’nor (no GIWF record) was left unconscious in the Figure Four Sleeper; the fed ruled a no contest (3:12).

name: GIWF Global — 17 Mar 1999

matches.note: E Razor’s bridging back suplex left both men’s shoulders down: a double pin (8:25).

notes: Unlisted bout: Peter Steele (led by Ole Gus) pinned The Adonis (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) after a Yakuza kick (6:17). Unlisted bout: Jason Parson (led by Angela Winston) pinned the debuting Nick Neon (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Falling Star (9:48).

name: GIWF Global — 23 Mar 1999

matches.note: GIWF Intercontinental Champion Shane Stone won by disqualification (7:45) when Cockney Rebel broke up his pin after the Huricane; Cockney Rebel and Hamish McGrubber (“The Clash”) then beat Stone down with a spike piledriver, the Last Orders and the Highland Fling.

notes: Unlisted bout: Curt Raines beat “The Ak-Attack” Christian Atkinson (no GIWF record; led to the ring by Lyndee Atkinson) with the Rainedrop DDT (7:32).

matches.note: Main event, billed as the GIWF’s first inter-gender match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: “The Raineman” Curt Raines, “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre and “Tornado” Shane Stone (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against MaK, “The Ace” Jason Parson and “Spicy” Angela Winston (led by Jorgy; Angela Winston has no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Hamish McGrubber hit Spectre with the Highland Fling outside and the Cockney Rebel attacked Stone; Lew Spectre was counted out and MaK, Parson and Winston won (16:52).

name: GIWF Global — 6 Apr 1999

matches.note: A lumberjack I Quit match (the Dreamwarriors, AmWt, Evil, Misled Youth, Armageddon and G-Lite around the ring), Richard Ray Vaughn in Spectre’s corner; the time limit expired with neither man quitting.
The North American Champion the Bum Boozler, with Gimp, and Krozor were both counted out.

The Mighty Israelites (billed Shylock and “The Mighty One” Solomon) beat Attitude Adjustment, the new pairing of Ozzy Douglas and Ian Ice; Solomon pinned Ice with the Holy Manna (8:30) on a count Ice protested as fast.

For the GIWF Intercontinental Championship. The Punisher came up through the ring, Lew Spectre, Richard Ray Vaughn and “Suave” Stevie West had the cage raised and climbed in; Spectre, in a referee’s shirt, counted Stone’s pin and the Youngbloods beat Cockney Rebel down before Hamish McGrubber speared Stone under the ring. The fed ruled a no contest.

notes: Unlisted bout: “The Ace” Jason Parson (the billing of the lineage’s jazon-parzon), led by Angela Winston, beat Eliminator of DarkSide (no GIWF record) with the Falling Star (8:50).

matches.note: The Mighty Israelites (Shylock and Solomon) beat Armageddon (Don Carson and Kendall Stripp); Solomon pinned Stripp after a belly-to-back superplex (5:47).

Advertised as Curt Raines v. Hamish McGrubber for the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship; Raines sent a doctor’s certificate and Lew Spectre, led by Richard Ray Vaughn, took his place. Raines, “here all along”, ran in and hit McGrubber with a chair; McGrubber chased him to the back and was counted out (7:10).
The Thompson Boys (Dan and Harry Thompson) beat Armageddon (Don Carson and Kendall Stripp) (5:42).

World Champion Curt Raines and Intercontinental Champion Shane Stone, with Richard Ray Vaughn, against the Clash (Cockney Rebel and Hamish McGrubber, with The Guv’nor and the Mitchell Brothers). Lew Spectre and The Punisher came to ringside and brawled with the Mitchell Brothers; while Stone distracted the referee a masked man low-blowed the Rebel, who was counted out (9:27).
For the GIWF World Television Championship. The time limit expired (15:44); Studog pinned Krozor after the bell and counted the fall himself, and the fed ruled a draw.

name: GIWF Global — 28 Apr 1999

matches.note: Misled Youth (Freak and Flammable; Flammable has no GIWF record) beat the Thompson Boys, billed here as “Dangerous Dan” and “Hardcore Harry”; Freak pinned Harry after a shooting star press through a table (13:10).

For the GIWF Intercontinental Championship: Pyro and Krozor brawled outside and were both counted out while Shane Stone laughed in the ring; the fed’s verdict was a double countout and Stone kept the title.

notes: Unlisted bout: Hamish McGrubber beat Jerry Wight (no GIWF record) in 1:45; Curt Raines then broke a baseball bat over McGrubber’s head. Unlisted bout: The Bum Boozler beat “Big Ed, The Ruthless Bastard” The Assassin (no GIWF record), led by Britney, by countout (6:00) after Physio Dave grabbed Britney; The Assassin then quit the GIWF and the Mutha Buckers. Unlisted bout: non-title-match Curt Raines beat Daemon (no GIWF record) in 0:28; Hamish McGrubber then laid Daemon out with the Highland Fling.

matches.note: Tag match, refereed by Dermott Gallagher, the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero, The Punisher and “Suave” Stevie West) in their debut as a team against Gangster Power (Franky Devlan and Nails Zanetti, led by “Chicago” Mike; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Cameron threw Zanetti out of the ring and he was counted out; the Phenomenons won (9:43).

Hell in a Cell, a long-standing feud: “The Canadian Rage” Cage against “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn). The introductions were cut off by “Ozzy Douglas” — Eric Cameron in a silicone mask; Spectre came out of the crowd with a steel cane and the Youngbloods (Spectre, Shane Stone, Eric Cameron, Richard Ray Vaughn and The Punisher) beat Cage down, Spectre powerbombing him from the top of the Cell through tables. The verdict: No Contest. Blade and Edge ran the Youngbloods off.

Armageddon (Don Carson and Kendall Stripp) against “The Ace” Jason Parson, with Angela Winston; all three were counted out after a fan at ringside attacked Carson and Stripp — the fed’s verdict was a double countout.
Referee Keith Burge stopped the bout after Henrique Escobar’s elbowsmash dropped John Constantine, and had Escobar taken out of the arena; the page gives no verdict.
The Bum Boozler’s mystery partner was Studog Escobar; Al Crud was counted out (6:32).
For the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship: Lew Spectre, with Richard Ray Vaughn, beat the champion Hamish McGrubber by countout (9:39), so the title did not change hands.

Tag team triangle match, refereed by Steven Lodge: Stone and Cameron (announced as the Phenomenons, led by Borrico Agujero, The Punisher and “Suave” Stevie West), the Cossack Warriors (Ivan and Yuri Kickabollockov, managed by Rasputin; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) and the debuting Swinging Hipsters (Mike Powers and Austin Myers, with Miss Piccadilly, thawed from blocks of ice). Eric Cameron eliminated Austin Myers with the Showstopper; Shylock swung a bag of Ducats into the back of Cameron’s head and Ivan Kickabollockov pinned Cameron after the Vodka flame breath. The Cossack Warriors won (7:34).

name: GIWF Global — 25 May 1999

matches.note: The Phenomenons, led by Borrico Agujero, The Punisher and “Suave” Stevie West, won by disqualification (4:49) when Yuri Kickabollockov rode a horse into Eric Cameron.

A masked man stepped out of the casket and knocked Lew Spectre out with a bat; The Iron Priest (twiztid) shut him in the casket and Evil strapped it shut and carried it out of the arena. The page gives no verdict.
For the GIWF World Television Title: Curt Raines beat The Iron Priest (twiztid’s aka), led by Cardinal Fang (6:56).

notes: Unlisted bout: cage-match Pyro beat Ice J (no GIWF record) (7:00); Misled Youth then buried Ice J under steel chairs. Unlisted bout: Studog Escobar, led by John Barnes, beat “Coldfire” Zach Shook (no GIWF record) (9:42).

name: GIWF Global — 15 Jun 1999

matches.note: Kevin Skinz’s debut (led by Mrs. Betty Skinz): both men were counted out, White Wolf landing a low blow at the count of nine (a double countout).
The Dreamwarriors beat the Swinging Hipsters (Mike Powers and Austin Myers, led by Miss Piccadilly) when Austin Myers submitted to John Constantine’s London Bridge (7:42).

notes: Unlisted bout: Ueshiba Kancho’s debut: he pinned “The Joker” Jimmy Callahan (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Hijishime Lock (2:10) while Akira watched from ringside. Unlisted bout: tag team match Misled Youth (Flammable, Freak and Mad Jack Manson) against the Cossack Warriors (Ivan and Yuri, led by ‘The Mad Monk’ Rasputin; no iwf/giwf/uwf record): their former trainer Alexei attacked the Cossacks; then the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, with Borrico Agujero) rode down on the Cossacks’ horses, laid out both teams with the Cyclone, the Phenomenal DDT and the Phenomenal Ending, and dragged them away tied to the horses. No contest.

matches.note: Tag match: the Mighty Israelites (Solomon and Shylock) against Gangster Power (Nails Zanetti and Franky Devlan, led by “Chicago” Mike). Shylock made Franky Devlan submit to the Holy Manna; the Mighty Israelites won (4:12).

“The Beautiful One” Daneel McCord against “Fatty” Kevin Skinz (led by his mother, Mrs Betty Skinz). Kitten distracted McCord and Ace Thunder, crawling out from under the ring, hit him with her stiletto heel; Skinz pinned him for his first win (6:02).

“Crash” Peter Steele (led by Ole Gus) against Brimstone (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Steele won with the Crash & Burn (3:42). Two masked men then attacked Brimstone and unmasked as Kendall Stripp and Don Carson — Armageddon returned.

For the GIWF Television Title: the champion “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn), in his first defence, against the Grim Reaper, an alternate for the injured Studog Escobar. Vaughn’s briefcase was intercepted and used on Spectre; Spectre won with the Figure-Four Sleeper (14:08).

Tag match, refereed by Graham Poll: the Swinging Hipsters (Mike Powers and Austin Myers, led by Miss Piccadilly) against the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero), a return match. Miss Piccadilly twice distracted the referee; the time limit expired as Eric Cameron covered Austin Myers after the Phenomenal Ending. The verdict: A Draw (10:00). Later in the night the Phenomenons came to ringside during the Dark Lords v. Misled Youth match and threw chairs.

Triangle match for three debutants, refereed by Graham Poll: Inferno ("From Boston, Mass... Weighing in at 210 pounds..."; no GIWF record), Vincenzo (no GIWF record) and D Dawg Benny-J. D Dawg Benny-J tagged out to Vincenzo, and Inferno pinned Vincenzo with the Stairway to Hell (5:31).

Tag match, refereed by Keith Burge: Misled Youth (Jack Manson and Freak) beat "The Brotherhood", Phoenix and Raven — Freak pinned Phoenix with a shooting star press (8:45). Phoenix is not filed in the side: which record this Phoenix is (the IWF's Phoenix, Jay Phoenix, or neither) is not settled.

Tag match against a masked "Mystery Team", refereed by Steven Lodge. The masked men laid Freak out and the referee was found unconscious; the first masked man unmasked as Phoenix (expecting his brother Raven, found taped to a chair backstage) and the second as the Undead Walker, and the bout dissolved into a brawl with David Rico, the Dark Lords and Misled Youth. No decision was given.

Lew Spectre, led to the ring by Richard Ray Vaughn, fought Ueshiba Kancho to a double countout: Vaughn distracted Kancho and Spectre hit two Reverse Cradle Piledrivers on the floor, but froze when the Global-Tron showed Hamish McGrubber arriving with the Cockney Rebel, and the referee counted both men out.

matches.stipulation: Main Event - North American Title Match
matches.note: For the GIWF North American Title, refereed by Graham Poll: the Cockney Rebel (c) against Inferno ("Hailing from Boston, Mass... Weighing in at 210 pounds..."; no GIWF record), unbeaten on his arrival. Inferno hit the Stairway to Hell twice and kept the champion on the floor, but after the Cockney Rebel's Last Orders the Global-Tron showed Hamish McGrubber being attacked backstage by the Youngbloods; the Rebel left the ring to help him, was tripped by David Rico, and the show went off the air with no decision given.

Tag match, refereed by Steven Lodge; the Phenomenons were led to the ring by Borrico Agujero, two days after Eric Cameron was run over by the Mighty Israelites at Global Warming. Daneel McCord came from under the ring and hit John Constantine with brass knuckles, and Shane Stone pinned Constantine with the Cyclone (9:26).
Refereed by Uriah Rennie. The Bum Boozler, led to the ring by Gimp, beat "The General" Mike Sandman, led to the ring by Dawn, by submission to the Bum Booz Bugger (7:07).

A 2-on-1 handicap match, refereed by Mike Reed: Joseph Rosso against Inferno and "Coldfire" Zach Shook (neither has a GIWF record); Rosso told the referee it would be no disqualification. Kitten slapped Rosso and hit him with a low blow from the floor, but Rosso made Inferno submit to the Flatliner Leg-Lock (7:53), and under the stipulation Inferno and Zach Shook left the GIWF. Afterwards David Rico hit Rosso with a lead pipe as Rosso went for Kitten.

Tag match: RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ) against the Brotherhood, billed “Phoenix and Raven”. Phoenix pinned J. Harold Christ with the Risen from the ashes; the Brotherhood won (6:11). Team Esco then sealed the arena doors and laid out Raven and Phoenix, marking them with spray-painted domino dots.

For the vacant GIWF Intercontinental Title: “The Corporal” Cpl. Punishment against “The Executioner” David Rico (led by David Head). The Youngbloods decided it: the lights went out, Lew Spectre and Eric Cameron drew the referee’s attention while Shane Stone hit Rico with the belt, and Cpl. Punishment pinned him after the Lethal Injection (7:12). Stone then “knighted” the Corporal as champion; Spectre, Stone and Cameron beat down Rico (the Phenomenal Ending) and the referee, and the Youngbloods left through the crowd with the title.

For the GIWF World Title: the champion Hamish McGrubber against Studog Escobar (led by John Barnes), Twiztid and Akira. Twiztid pinned Akira; McGrubber pinned Twiztid with the Highland Fling; the referee stopped the fight on McGrubber after 180 seconds and Studog Escobar became World Champion (24:15).
First round of the tag-title tournament: Misled Youth (Freak and Jack Manson) beat Asylum (Black Dragon and Darkside) when Freak’s shooting star press pinned Black Dragon (5:54).
For the Intercontinental Title (Commissioner Williams’s “Rocky Challenge”): a double countout; Cpl. Punishment kept the title.

First round of the GIWF World Tag Team Title tournament: the Dreamwarriors (Sandman and John Constantine), former champions, against Underground (Da Heat and Abdul Rahaman, led by Carl Big). Da Heat pinned John Constantine with the Sewer Side Suplex; Underground won (11:57) and went on to the quarter-final battle royal. The Fomorians then laid out Underground and Carl Big.

“The Canadian Luchadore” Deke Aurora (with Nephilim and Angelique) against El Leon, Joshua Dillinger’s masked billing. A masked man in El Leon’s mask pulled the referee from the ring during Aurora’s pin; the referee called for the bell and Aurora was given the match (11:28). El Leon then drove Aurora through a table with a Stardust Press.
Hell in a Cell match: Pyro against “Unseen” White Wolf. White Wolf pinned Pyro after two Frankensteiners (28:53).

“Superstar” Ace Thunder (led by Kitten) against “The Jedi Master” Al Crud. The time limit expired and the match went on; Hamish McGrubber came to the ring, Crud argued with him, and Crud pinned Ace with the Mother Crudder (23:07).

Triangle match for a TV title shot at Sunday Afternoon Suicide: Lyle Wile, Nephilim (with Angelique) and Stevie May — May was laid out on the ramp by two men before the bell and never entered, so it was fought one on one. The Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron) came looking for their tag-team belts: Cameron handcuffed Angelique and superkicked the referee, and the two beat down Nephilim, Lyle Wile and Deke Aurora; the referee came to in time to see the Phenomenal Ending and called for the DQ; Nephilim was given the match (7:57). Stevie West brought the Phenomenons new “Universal” belts.

Main event, title v. title for the GIWF North American and Intercontinental Championships: the Intercontinental Champion Cpl. Punishment (led by Richard Ray Vaughn, who dragged in the bound Guv’nor) against the North American Champion Cockney Rebel, with the interim Commissioner Lew Spectre as special guest referee and lumberjacks chosen by the Phenomenons (“a twig, an autumn leaf, a cigarette butt …”). Spectre tripped the Rebel and pushed him off the ladder; Eric Cameron and Shane Stone ran in and were cattle-prodded; when the Rebel reached the belts Spectre called for the bell and disqualified him for hitting the referee — Cpl. Punishment won (17:38). The Rebel took the belts anyway and brawled with Spectre.

name: GIWF Global — 15 Sep 1999

matches.note: Asylum (Black Dragon and Darkside) against Misled Youth (Freak and Jack Manson): a double countout.

For the GIWF Television Title, made a triple threat after Ben Jackson broke up the eight-man battle royal for the title shot: Lyle Wile (with the Ring Rats) pinned Stevie May with the Facelift and took the title from Nephilim (10:07).
For the Intercontinental Title: the time limit expired; Cpl. Punishment kept the title.

notes: Unlisted bout: tag-team match First round of the North American tag-title tournament, made a handicap match after the Fomorians threw Da Heat through a tour bus window: Tropical Storm (Miguel Lanza and Jamie Dermott) beat Abdul Rahaman of Underground (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) alone, Lanza’s Reef Dive Driver getting the pin (5:13).

matches.note: First round of the North American Tag-Titles tournament, refereed by Graham Poll: the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey) against Shades of Hell (Damien and Wolf X, led by Destructive Everything; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Tethra pinned Damien; the Fomorians won (9:50) and went through to the semi-finals.

White Wolf (champion) against “The Fallen One” Nephilim (led by Angelique), refereed by Uriah Rennie. With White Wolf out cold on the floor, the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron) ran down and tried to carry off Angelique; Tropical Storm, Shades of Hell and Nephilim chased them, Nephilim caned Cameron, and neither man made it back to the ring. The verdict: A DOUBLE COUNTOUT.

matches.stipulation: six man tag team triangle match
matches.note: Main event, refereed by Steven Lodge: David, Guy and Marc Rico (the Eurofighters and “The Executioner” David Rico, led by David Head) against Lew Spectre and the Phenomenons, Shane Stone and Eric Cameron (led by Richard Ray Vaughn and Borrico Agujero), against Twiztid with RIMJOB, Schmitt and J. Harold Christ (the Eurofighters have no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Joshua Dillinger and Titan brought baseball bats to ringside and threw them to Cameron and Stone; the referee called for the bell and Stone broke a bat across Guy Rico’s head. No result was announced.
Opening match: Devils Disciple against Daredevil (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), both beaten in their debuts at the weekend. Daredevil submitted to the Devils Decider (3:13).
Ueshiba Kancho, after losing the North American Title at Quake, against Jack Leer (“the Smutman”; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Kancho pinned Leer after the Black Feather Lock (4:25).

For the GIWF World Television Title: the champion “Unforgiven” Ben Jackson (Ben Jericho’s billing; a registry aka) against Angel (“From Rio de Janeiro, Brazil… 300 pounds”). With Angel’s figure-four on and the referee blinded by smoke, Deke Aurora appeared on the top turnbuckle and hit Angel with the Aurora Borealis; Jackson pinned Angel after the Unforgiven DDT and retained (6:03).

For the GIWF World Tag-Team Championships: the champions “The Canadian Luchadore” Deke Aurora and “The Fallen One” Nephilim (led by Angelique) against RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ, accompanied by Ace Thunder). Borrico Agujero rode Vejiga de la Billis down and trampled Ace Thunder; while Aurora and Christ dealt with Agujero, Shane Stone and Eric Cameron came out of the crowd, laid out Nephilim (the Cyclone), Triple J (the Showstopper) and the referee (the Phenomenal Ending), draped the two men over each other and made a second referee, dragged down from the back, count: “Nephilim and Triple J pinned each other!” Both teams were announced as the winners; Stone and Cameron left with the World tag team title belts.
Opening match between two newcomers: Tremor (from Dundee) against Matthew Kidman (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Tremor pinned Kidman after the Destruction Drop (3:37).

The tag-team debut of the New Era — Angel and Sebastian Lopez (Lopez and the team have no iwf/giwf/uwf record) — against the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey). Tethra pinned Lopez after the Kissing the Blarny Stone; the Fomorians won (9:30).

“The Texas Playboy” Josh Dillinger (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), the number-one contender for the Television Title, against “Superstar” Stevie May. Dillinger pinned May after the Leon-Tamer Moonsault (4:41).

Main event, for the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship: the champion Twiztid against “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) — the leaders of the Order of the Hammer and of the Youngbloods. Vaughn distracted Twiztid again and again; they fought outside the ring and were both counted out: the verdict was a double countout, and Twiztid kept the title.
The first of a three-match series between Devils Disciple and Angel (“From Rio de Janeiro, Brazil… 300 pounds”). Angel pinned Devils Disciple after a second Heaven & Hell (5:29).

Tag match: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero), with Cameron back from his claimed paralysis, against the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey). Stone hit the Cyclone on Tethra for a near fall; Tethra pinned Cameron after the Kissing the Blarny Stone and the Fomorians won (9:28).

Billed “Pete Steele & ??? -v- RIMJOB”: “Crash” Peter Steele (led by Ole Gus) came out with no partner and wrestled RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ) alone. Triple J pinned Steele after the Tombstone; RIMJOB won (16:22).

Mr. Meaner (Ezra Kazee, whose registry akas include “Mr. Meaner”) against Angel (“Fighting out of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil… 300 pounds”), each heading into Halloween Hell. Meaner submitted to the Heaven & Hell; Angel won (4:25).

Devils Disciple (led by The Gremlin) against Shark, back after Pretty in the City’s oxygen-tank attack at Sunday Afternoon Suicide; Daneel and Mark McCord came to ringside with the dented tank. Shark pinned Devils Disciple after a fisherman’s suplex (6:19).

Triangle match, refereed by Steven Lodge: Angel (“Fighting out of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil… 300 pounds”) against Devils Disciple (led by The Gremlin) against Grim Reaper. The Reaper took out the referee with a chair, stood at Angel’s side, then smashed the chair into Angel’s knee and went after it with his Skull Staff; he also chaired Devils Disciple. No result was given.

Ladder cage tag match: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero) against RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ). The Phenomenons’ Universal Tag Team belts hung from Bob the Robot and RIMJOB’s Eddie the Pygmy above the ring; Lew Spectre and Corporal Punishment took over the cell controls; Stone sunset-flip powerbombed Christ from the ladder, Cameron hit a Shooting Star Press from the top, and Stone retrieved Bob the Robot. The Phenomenons won (13:48).

Tag match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Pretty in the City (Daneel and Mark McCord; Mark McCord has no iwf/giwf/uwf record) against the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey), Ace Thunder on commentary. Fey stood on the stacked McCords and Eriu had the referee count; the Fomorians won (5:39). Slapshot attacked the McCords afterwards.

“Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against “The Celtic Knight” Bres (led by Fey), refereed by Uriah Rennie. Fey tossed Bres a nutcracker and he knocked Spectre down with it, but the McCords came from under the ring, Mark kicked Fey and Daneel speared the referee before the count; the Knightmare Brigade (Ben Jackson, Tremor, Ashley Broad) attacked the McCords and the Phenomenons ran in. No result was given.

For the GIWF North American Tag-Titles, refereed by Mike Reed: the champions Tropical Storm (Miguel Lanza and Jamie Dermott) against the Outcastz (Barry Jones and Ben Wallace, led by Crazy Craig; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Miguel Lanza scored the pin; Tropical Storm retained (8:47).

First match of the GIWF Television Title tournament, refereed by Graham Barber: Devils Disciple (led by The Gremlin) against the Masked Demon (led by El Mask; no iwf/giwf/uwf record), in only his second match. Devils Disciple won with the Devils Decider (5:19).

A 3-on-1 handicap loser-leaves-town match, refereed by Graham Barber: Shark against Kevin Skinz, Dark Phoenix and “The Ultimate Wrecking Machine” Sebastian Lopez (Dark Phoenix and Lopez have no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Shark piled up his opponents and pinned all three at once (6:49). Three masked men then drugged Shark with a dart and carried him away.

matches.stipulation: Francis On A Pole tag team match
matches.note: Francis on a Pole tag match (the only way to win: climb the pole and retrieve the remains of Francis the Skunk), refereed by Uriah Rennie: Pretty in the City (Daneel and Mark McCord; Mark McCord has no iwf/giwf/uwf record) against the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero). Stone clotheslined the referee by mistake; RIMJOB’s J. Harold Christ swung the bound Borrico Agujero into Stone and Triple J hit Cameron with Bob the Robot, both Phenomenons left bleeding; the McCords looked at the pole and walked out. No result was given.

Refereed by Danny Davis: Tremor beat the debuting The Rattler (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Destruction Drop (4:15). The North-South Express and Joshua Dillinger then beat the Rattler down and dressed him in a diaper.

Tag match, refereed by Earl Hebner: the North-South Express (Jose Juarez and Jean du Pont, led by Joshua Dillinger) beat the debuting Wizards of Odds (Mike Van Token and Buddy Green, led by Mary Jane; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when Jose Juarez pinned Buddy Green after El Machete (3:44). Scorpion then attacked the Wizards of Odds with a baseball bat.

Refereed by Danny Davis: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) beat the stripped former World Champion Twiztid when the Figure-Four Sleeper put him out (12:55), after Corporal Punishment’s interference, the Phenomenons’ distractions of Tropical Storm and the Phenomenons’ attack on Ace Thunder. Spectre and the Corporal left with the World title belt.

Cage match, refereed by Graham Poll: Mike Sandman (led by Dawn) beat “the Northern Star” Stuart Price (led by Jonny Polo; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) by escaping over the top of the cage while Price fell from it (13:31).

Triangle match between three debuting wrestlers, refereed by Uriah Rennie: “The Odd” Hardcore Oddy (led by Jess), The Firestarter and “The Deathbringer” Hexon (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). While Jess argued with the referee Oddy broke his guitar over the Firestarter’s head and pinned him (11:06). The Firestarter’s “Inferno” here is his finishing move (not a person).

Handicap match, refereed by Nelson Steel: Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against the World Tag Team Champions Law & Order (Studog Escobar and Cpl. Punishment). Lyle Wile ran in, turned on Law & Order with a chair and the Facelift on Studog and dragged Spectre over him; Spectre won by pinfall and Wile joined the “New” Youngbloods. The Shark then attacked Spectre. Earlier that day Spectre had released Shane Stone and Eric Cameron from the Youngbloods.

Non-title prelude to the March Maelstrom II Intercontinental Title match, refereed by Nelson Steel: Lyle Wile beat Mr. Meaner (Ezra Kazee; the man who held the Intercontinental belt without being its champion) with the Facelift (11:03).

Backlot Brawl triangle match, fought in the alley behind the arena: Rage (with Jennifer), The Masked Man (with Speaker) and Killer Dude. Pete Steele leapt from the fire escape onto Killer Dude and Rage; he and The Masked Man threw both men into a dumpster, Speaker brought gasoline and Pete Steele set it alight. No decision was announced.
For the GIWF Television Title: champion Fagen (led by Sadie) retained against “The Innovator of Violence” Pogo when referee Mike Reed stopped the fight on the Withering Faith (11:03).

Wolfgang Einenfaust of the 4th Reich against Killer Dude. While Wolfgang distracted the referee, Henrich Olberson struck Killer Dude with the timekeeper’s bell; a masked figure then dropkicked Olberson and superkicked Wolfgang, and Killer Dude got the pin (3:45).
Ezra Kazee pinned Wolfgang Einenfaust (6:43) after Gunta Steinmarch hit Kazee with a chair and a masked figure powerbombed Einenfaust.
A double countout; afterwards hooded monks chained Pogo to a Celtic Cross and carried him out.
Lew Spectre, led by Richard Ray Vaughn, made Gary Clark submit to the Figure-Four Sleeper (13:32), held on after the bell, then poured gasoline over Clark and set him alight.
Ben Jackson pinned Deke Aurora with the Unforgiven DDT (18:23); Law & Order and the Bringers of Darkness stood on the apron to keep the Order out.
First round of the GIWF Television Title tournament: Taff (led by Zeta; Thirteen under a new name) against Mike Sandman. Sandman won by submission with the Dream Time (14:16).

name: GIWF Global — 28 Jun 2000

matches.note: Billed by the commentary as a loser-leaves-town match: Law & Order beat the 4th Reich (Henrich Olberson and Gunta Steinmarch) (16:12) after the returning Angel, masked, and Major Payne fought off the rest of the Reich; Corporal Punishment and Studog Escobar pinned both men.
White Wolf beat “Naitch” Taff (Thirteen’s new ring name), led by Zeta, with the Artic Splash (15:04).

Lew Spectre, led by Richard Ray Vaughn, cradled Ben Jackson (12:46) after Tremor pulled the referee’s leg to break Jackson’s pin; afterwards Spectre crushed Jackson’s knee in a chair and doused him in gasoline to draw out Pete Steele, who gave Vaughn and Jackson the Crash n Burn and set Jackson alight. Earlier Spectre, Vaughn and Lyle Wile beat down the Masked Man in the parking lot.

notes: Unlisted bout: The rematch: Pogo beat B-Z (billed “BZ”; no GIWF record) with the Innovator of Violence (12:08).

matches.note: Singles debut, refereed by Uriah Rennie; billed as Inferno ("Hailing from Death Valley, Texas... Weighing in at 220 pounds..."). Inferno pinned "Viper" Jayson Fury (no GIWF record) with the Meltdown (8:22). White Wolf then appeared and spared him, and Evil came to the ring hunting him for his self-elimination at Infested Waters; Inferno hit Evil with the timekeeper's chair and escaped through the crowd.

Tag match, refereed by Nelson Steel: Irish Hood (Cluney C. and Jack Blarney) lost to The Apocalypse (Richard Gordon and Steven Fredericks, led by Dave 'The Chain' Roberts; no GIWF record), when Richard Gordon pinned Jack Blarney with the Decimator (12:36).

A forfeit (time 0:00:00): the New Youngbloods, Lyle Wile and Lew Spectre, came out still bandaged from Infested Waters, and Lew Spectre told the crowd there was no chance the match was happening; the Dark Lords were given the win.

The Phenomenons, now the Commissioners of the GIWF Tag Team Division, "drafted" Killer Dude into the tag division and gave him a mystery partner: a masked seven-and-a-half-foot figure who turned out to be Borrico Agujero on stilts, handing Killer Dude a miniature golf club. Refereed by Graham Poll; the Phenomenons won by disqualification (14:19) when Killer Dude struck Eric Cameron low with the club.

matches.stipulation: Ladder/Cage Match for the THC Title

matches.note: Refereed by Nelson Steel. "The Common Man" Ezra Kazee pinned "EZ-Punk" Johnny Bravo (no GIWF record) with the Bomb de Commonwealth (6:07), and offered him his hand afterwards.

A 4-on-1 tag handicap match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Lew Spectre, led to the ring by Richard Ray Vaughn, against NRG (Steve and Michael Collins) and Random Acts of Violence (Maim and Torture; no GIWF record), led by Conor Fitzgerald. Vaughn threw Spectre the briefcase; when Steve Collins went to break up Spectre's Figure-Four Sleeper on Michael Collins, Maim and Torture turned on their partners, and Michael Collins submitted (10:58). Afterwards Ben Jackson, as "Unforgiven", laid Spectre out with the Unforgiven DDT and announced himself special referee of Spectre's World Title match at Global Warming.

Tag match, refereed by Nelson Steel: the Vallhallans (Vespasien and Angelus, led by Sophia) beat the debuting Manglers (introduced as "The Maulers": Benjamin Lewis and Marc Wolper; no GIWF record), Angelus pinning Benjamin Lewis with the Forgiven Sins (12:24).

Refereed by Uriah Rennie; billed as Inferno ("From Death Valley, Texas..."). Inferno pinned Angel, back from time away, with the Meltdown (20:17). Afterwards Christian Goodwill, a new signing, powerbombed Angel off the ramp, and Inferno came back into the ring and speared Goodwill.

Refereed by Nelson Steel. The Judge lost to Taff (Thirteen, under the ring name he took in June 2000), led to the ring by Zeta, who shoved The Judge off the turnbuckle and twice hit him with a chair; The Judge submitted to Taff’s Unlucky Number (11:56).
Refereed by Uriah Rennie. "The Innovator of Violence" Pogo pinned Cypher (no GIWF record) with the Innovator of Violence (6:30).

Tag match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Vallhallans (Vespasien and Angelus, led by Sophia) against Law & Order (Studog Escobar and Corporal Punishment). Studog Escobar made Angelus submit to the Lethal Injection (13:14). It was billed as a number-one contenders' match for the World Tag-Team Titles; before the next bout the Phenomenons, as Commissioners of the Tag Team Division, vacated those titles and ruled that it had been for the number-one seed in the tournament for them.

Tag match refereed by Uriah Rennie, with the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron) as guest referees: Killer Dude and Onslaught, led by The Watcher, against “Naitch” Taff (Thirteen, under his new ring name), led by Zeta, and the Shark, the partner Taff had picked. Before the bell Lew Spectre and Lyle Wile laid out the Shark with a sledgehammer and the Figure Four Sleeper, and Taff wrestled alone for most of the match. The time limit expired and the referee let it continue; the Shark staggered back, tagged himself in, hit Deep Sea Carnage on Killer Dude and pinned him, Shane Stone counting the three (22:54).

Refereed by Graham Poll; billed as Inferno ("From Death Valley, Texas... Weighing in at 220 pounds..."). Christian Goodwill came in as the Television Champion. After the referee was knocked down, Goodwill beat on Inferno with a steel chair; Angel appeared on the ramp, hit Goodwill with the Heaven and Hell, stood the referee up and had Inferno make the pin (14:20). Global Warming 2000's commentary records this bout as the night Goodwill lost the Television title to Inferno. Afterwards Deke Aurora attacked Goodwill.

Main event, for the GIWF North American Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Mike Reed: the Dark Lords (Gabriel and Evil) against the champions, the Bringers of Darkness (Onslaught and Venom, led by The Watcher). The time limit expired and the referee let the match continue; Gabriel pinned Onslaught with the Fall from Grace (24:37) and the Dark Lords took the titles.

name: GIWF Global — 9 Aug 2000

matches.note: “Naitch” Taff (Thirteen’s new ring name), led by Zeta, beat The Judge when the referee stopped the fight in the Unlucky Number (8:00).
The Phenomenons, led by Borrico Agujero, beat the Vallhallans (led by Sophia) when Eric Cameron pinned Vespasien with the Showstopper (10:39).

Designated a cage match (escape to win): Deke Aurora, the Intercontinental Champion, climbed out after the Northern Lights Driver (19:41). Backstage the Crimson Ghost (identity not given on the page) attacked the Firestarter and Lew Spectre.

First leg of the Shark’s gauntlet for Lew Spectre’s GIWF World Heavyweight Title (his career at stake; Lyle Wile absent), Tremor the special referee and the Firestarter the enforcer: the Shark made The Prodigy pass out in the Great White Bite (8:12).
Second leg: Deke Aurora attacked before the bell; the Shark made him pass out in the Great White Bite (14:11).

Final leg, for Lew Spectre’s GIWF World Heavyweight Title: the Shark had Spectre out in the Great White Bite but held his arm up to stop the count, tied the belt around Spectre’s waist and had Tremor count him out, leaving the GIWF; the fed announces “The New Youngbloods” as the winners (35:25). Spectre retained; Richard Ray Vaughn was ejected from ringside by the Firestarter.

notes: Unlisted bout: Pole-tag team match Billed as a Cat-o-Nine-Tails on a pole match against Whip-Lash (Stitch and Scab, led by Miss Tress; no GIWF record). No result: Luca on L.U.C.A.B.O.T and the Dark Lords (Gabriel, Evil) stopped the bout, Evil knocked out the referee, and the Apocalypse (Decimation and Elimination) beat down the Dragoons and Whip-Lash with lead pipes.

matches.note: Tag match and the Don't Brothers' debut, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Don't Brothers (Dave and Dudley Don't, managed by Misty Misery) lost to Apocalypse (Richard Gordon and Steven Fredericks; no GIWF record) when Steven Fredericks pinned Dudley Don't after a flying elbowdrop (12:06).

Refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Television Champion Ezra Kazee against Luca the Imp inside L.U.C.A.B.O.T, a robot suit of over 400 pounds of steel (billed "L.U.C.A.B.O.T (w/Luca)", "Fighting out the famous Dark Lords Stable"). LUCABOT pinned Kazee with the LUCABOT_CLAP (14:49); moments later Luca, celebrating in the cockpit, set the robot to "White Wolf mode" by accident and it handed the Television title back to Kazee, which the commentators called vacated and returned to him.

Main event, refereed by Graham Poll; billed as Inferno, against Ben Jackson ("Unforgiven", filed under ben-jericho). The winner earned a match with Deke Aurora at the Northern Lights pay-per-view. The time limit expired and the referee let the match continue; Inferno pinned Jackson with the Meltdown (22:16).

For the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, with The Prodigy as special guest referee: Hybrid sprayed Al Crud in the eyes and pinned him with the Exclamation Mark while The Prodigy was down, but The Prodigy refused to raise his hand and ordered the match to continue; Al Crud retained (14:19).
Refereed by Nelson Steel: Craig Wright (called “Craig White” by the commentators) pinned “The Attacker in the Dark” Mad Man Max with an inside cradle (10:47).
Refereed by Isaiah Haywood: “Baby Lucas” Trent Lucas beat “The One” Spectacular Stu Stuart (led by Ann the Automaton; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Spotlight (10:17).

For the GIWF Television Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: “Superstar” Alexander Sebastian Saunders, in his first GIWF match, beat the champion Benito Cavalera (led by Massimilano Cavalera) with the Heartbreaker (13:57) and became the Television Champion.

Main event, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Phenomenons, Shane Stone and Eric Cameron (billed “The GIWF World Tag Team Champions”, led by Borrico Agujero with a detained Gary Clark), against L.U.C.A.B.O.T, Luca the Imp in the cockpit, for the North American Tag Team Title belts LUCABOT held. The Phenomenons called in Krushing Time, Dallas Culture and Brett Alpine, the Renegades II and the Lynch Mob; Francis the Skunk drove LUCABOT off, the Phenomenons pried the belts out of its chest, and Dallas Culture and Brett Alpine made off with them. The referee ruled it a no contest.
North American Tag Team Title Tournament, first round: Too Smutty lost to the Lynch Mob (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) (7:55).
For the GIWF Television Title: Hybrid pinned the champion, Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third, to win the title (15:47).

For the GIWF Television Title: champion Hybrid against Craig Wright (led by Linzi). The returning Joe Kenny had Wright hold Hybrid in a full nelson and hit Hybrid with a chair, then hit Wright with it as he went for the pin and rolled Hybrid on top; Hybrid retained (14:45).

For the GIWF North American Title: The Prodigy defended against Miss Pain (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), after Gary Clark came out with a contract from Jae O’Connor; The Prodigy won by pinfall after the boot to the face and a guillotine legdrop.

North American Tag Team Title Tournament quarter-final, refereed by Isiah Haywood: the Hardcore Elements (Roadkill Grill and Overturned Car) beat the Bushmen (Bigfoot and Sasquatch, led to the ring by Yeti; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when Roadkill Grill pinned Sasquatch after the Roadkill Cafe (9:38).

Main event, a triangle match refereed by Uriah Rennie: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) beat “Crash” Pete Steele (led by Ole Gus) and Celest. Unforgiven took Celest out on the stage with a Singapore cane and a straight-jacket German suplex, a man in a Big Bird costume attacked Steele, and Spectre won with the figure four when Steele, reaching toward the entrance for Al Crud, let his hand fall (22:33).

Refereed by Isiah Haywood: “The Hardcore Icon” Ace Thunder, in his first match in over a year, against EZ-Punk (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Ace rolled under the ring at the count of three and came back at nine refreshed and in a different shirt, then won with the Thunderclap (6:58).

Tag match refereed by Uriah Rennie: the R.P.A (Skull and Deck) against the #1 contenders the Hooded Perverts (Tommo and Ched, led by Dirty Dave). No decision was given: Red Bull cans felled Ched and Tommo, the Masked Red Bull Destroyer unmasked as Trent Lucas, the Connection (Mike Montgomery, ICK, Craig Wright) came through the crowd, and the R.P.A raked the Perverts with cheese graters and joined the Connection.

GIWF Television Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: Ice Cold Killa (c) against “Crash” Peter Steele (led by Ole Gus). Craig Wright came out with a chair, quit the Connection and hit ICK with it; the Connection threw Wright into a wheelie bin. Pete Steele won with the Crash & Burn (15:17), the new Television Champion.
Refereed by Graham Poll: Konrad Karter lost to “The Sarge” Sgt. Sledjhamma (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), pinned after the Lights Out (7:48).

Billed as “CHL -v- The Dragoons”, refereed by Isiah Haywood. As the Dragoons set up a win, the Global-Tron showed the Don’t Brothers — whom the commentators call the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores — tied to chairs; the masked “CHL#1” and “CHL#2” hit a Shinzaki Bomb for the pin (7:31) and unmasked after the bell as Star Motion (“The Vulture” Dallas Culture and Brent Alpine).

appearances.note: Billed “Gary Clark -v- Lyle Wile -v- The Prodigy” at the foot of the card (805), “More to follow ...” — the bout’s text was never written.
Billed “Jay Phoenix -v- Celest” at the foot of the card (807), “More to follow ...” — the bout’s text was never written.
Billed “Gary Clark -v- Lyle Wile -v- The Prodigy” at the foot of the card (805), “More to follow ...” — the bout’s text was never written.
Billed “Gary Clark -v- Lyle Wile -v- The Prodigy” at the foot of the card (805), “More to follow ...” — the bout’s text was never written.

matches.note: Tag match refereed by Nelson Steel: the estranged Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero) against Star Motion (Brent Alpine and Dallas Culture). Shane Stone went to tag; Eric Cameron stuck his tongue out, took a giant crème pie from Borrico Agujero and hit his partner in the face with it, and Brent Alpine rolled Shane Stone up (12:32).
Refereed by Graham Poll: the Television Champion The Plague (led by Evan McCann) beat “The Sarge” Sgt. Sledjhamma (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Black Death (10:10).

Billed as “Luca -v- Celest”, a World Heavyweight Title match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: L.U.C.A.B.O.T. (c; Luca the Imp’s robot) against Celest. As Celest seemed to tap to the Pneumatic Nut Crush, a chain from the ceiling took out the referee and an anchor dropped by Pete Steele (with Ole Gus in the rafters) shattered the cockpit; Pete Steele chased Luca into the crowd. No decision was given.

Refereed by Nelson Steel: the GIWF World Tag-Team Champions the RPA (Skull and Deck) against Star Motion (Brent Alpine and Dallas Culture), the title not at stake. Brent Alpine pinned Skull with the Shining Light (12:17). The Dragoons then attacked both teams with chairs and put Star Motion through tables.

For the GIWF Intercontinental Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: Jay Phoenix (champion) against Ace Thunder. Slasher ran in with a barbed-wire chair and hit Ace Thunder as he went for a swinging DDT; Jay Phoenix hit the Meltdown and pinned him (14:42).

Main event, non-title, refereed by Nelson Steel: the Prodigy against the World Heavyweight Champion Luca in LUCABOT. Gary Clark came through the crowd and brawled with the Prodigy, and Lyle Wile came to ringside; the match was ruled a no contest (11:42).

For the GIWF Television Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: Craig Wright (“From Grangemouth, Scotland”) against the champion the Plague, led to the ring by Evan McCann. The Plague pinned Wright with the Black Death (9:16).

Main event, a tag match refereed by Isiah Haywood: Celest and Jay Phoenix against Al Crud and Pete Steele, led to the ring by Ole Gus, both still hurt from March Maelstrom. Jay Phoenix pinned Pete Steele with a twisting moonsault (19:59). Afterwards Hardkore (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) ran in and hit both brothers, who were laughing at him, with the Hardkore Sleepwalker.
Refereed by Isiah Haywood: Mike Montgomery beat “Small Fry” Prime (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Hangman’s Joke (12:05).

For the GIWF Intercontinental Title, refereed by Graham Poll: Jay Phoenix (champion; “Fighting out of Death Valley, Texas”) against Konrad Karter, who had won the title shot in the March Maelstrom battle royal. Jay Phoenix pinned Karter with the Meltdown (19:40); Karter complained of a fast count. Earlier in the night Jay Phoenix and Celest had attacked Bob Roberts, Hector, the Hooded Perverts, Craig Wright, Pete Steele, Ole Gus and Luca backstage and in the arena.

Ki’s debut, refereed by Isiah Heywood: “King Kill” Ki against “THE MAN” Lee Coulter. Ki fetched the ring bell and hit Coulter with it in front of the referee, was disqualified, kept beating Coulter with the bell and hit the referee with it too. The winner by disqualification: Lee Coulter (0:08:20).

Tag team match refereed by Graham Poll: the Hardcore Elements (Roadkill Grill and Overturned Car) beat the R.P.A. (Skull and Deck), fresh from the cash Microsoft’s Mr. Hicks handed them. Roadkill Grill pinned Deck after the Roadkill Cafe (0:04:11).

For the GIWF TV Title, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the champion The Plague (led by Evan McCann) against CHL #1 of the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores (no character record; the title history holds him unminted, reign giwf-television-r065). Jaxx interrupted to challenge The Plague to a ladder match and threw TNT off the stage; then CHL #2 and CHL #3 ran in, and while one distracted the referee the others hit the Cybernetic Hardcore Hurricanrana and the Cybernetic Suplex ’01 and a Luchadore pinned The Plague: “The Winner: The Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadore” (0:12:14), the new Television Champion. Afterwards the Forces of Darkness threw The Plague through chairs and into a dumpster and set it alight.

Four corners tag team match, refereed by Danny Davis, to decide the Extreme Prejudice challengers for the World and North American Tag Team Titles. Before the bell the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron) ran in and dragged Star Motion (Brent Alpine and Dallas Culture) away as their “new tag team partners”, so the bout was three-way: the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores (CHL #2 and CHL #3) against the Hardcore Elements (Roadkill Grill and Overturned Car) and the Dragoons (Bahamut and Tiamat; Tiamat has no iwf/giwf/uwf record). CHL #2 eliminated the Hardcore Elements (German Suplex on Overturned Car) and then Bahamut; the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores won (0:12:29) and earned the World Tag Team Title shot.

Television Title bout refereed by Tim White: the new champion CHL #1 of the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores (no character record; the title history holds him unminted) against Mike Montgomery of the Forces of Darkness. The Plague watched from the ramp; Prime came through the crowd with a sledgehammer, hit Montgomery and then CHL #1, and laid Montgomery on top of the champion: Montgomery won the title by pinfall (0:06:35) — reign giwf-television-r066.

Six-man main event (billed as a tag team four corners match): Al Crud, Gurgles and Pete Steele against the Prodigy, Celest and Jay Phoenix. Evil of the Dark Lords came down first to tell Jay Phoenix he would settle their score at the pay-per-view, and left. In the ring Celest and Jay Phoenix refused every tag from the Prodigy and dropped off the apron; Gurgles caught the Prodigy in the Big Top and the Prodigy tapped out. Afterwards Celest and Pete Steele brawled, Jay Phoenix fought Crud and Gurgles (Crud’s forearm hit Gurgles), and the Prodigy added himself to the Extreme Prejudice World Title match.

Refereed by Des Galpin: “KJ” Kilo Jones against Ki (“King Kill”, of Watts, California). Kilo Jones won by pinfall with the Overdose (0:08:06), then went out to the parking lot and wrecked the Prodigy’s limousine with a baseball bat.

Non-title tag team match refereed by Isiah Heywood: the World Tag Team Champions the Forces of Darkness (Jared Crafter and Riggs; Riggs has no iwf/giwf/uwf record) against the Serial Thrillers (Gabriel Talbot and Adrian Devlin). CHL #2 and CHL #3 joined the broadcast table, tripped Crafter and walked off with the World Tag Team Title belts; Crafter pinned Talbot with the Soul Stealer (0:11:15).

For the GIWF Television Title, refereed by Luke Hutton: the champion “THE MAN” Lee Coulter against The Plague (led by Evan McCann). During the bout Jaxx appeared on the Global-Tron with TNT nailed to a locker-room wall, and Slasher dropped a cinder block on TNT’s head; The Plague left the ring and ran backstage to his stable-mate, and was counted out. The winner: Lee Coulter (0:09:12).

Main event tag team match refereed by Nelson Steel: the Bringers of Darkness (Venom and Onslaught, led by the Watcher) against Jay Phoenix and Celest, the Hatchett Brothers. Celest tagged Jay Phoenix in and Phoenix carried much of the bout against Venom and Onslaught before tagging Celest back in. Pete Steele, who had spent the night firebombing locker rooms looking for the brothers, charged out with a baseball bat and a Molotov cocktail and set the ring on fire; the Bringers bailed out, Steele cracked Jay Phoenix in the back with the bat (security then hit Phoenix with a fire extinguisher) and beat Celest down, and Jay Phoenix fought the flames with an extinguisher. No decision was announced.
Refereed by Jacob Jeremis: Konrad Karter of the Forces of Darkness lost to the debuting “The Bullet” Keflon (Paul Cannon; no iwf/giwf/uwf record), pinned after the Bullet Bomb (8:44).
Refereed by Uriah Rennie: Slasher and “Small Fry” Prime (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) brawled outside and were both counted out.
Refereed by Nelson Steel: “The Little Big Man” Trent Lucas beat “TNT” Tommy N Taylor (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Spotlight (14:05).

Main event, refereed by Isiah Heywood: “A.S.S.” Alexander Sebastian Saunders the third beat a debuting opponent billed “The Main Event” (no iwf/giwf/uwf record; name withheld) with the Shake-Spear (13:46).

Refereed by Isiah Heywood: Killer Dude beat Ki (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Killer Smash (6:13). After the bell the Elements of Destruction came out (TNT with a chair, the Plague with a sledgehammer); TNT struck Ki with the chair, the Plague handed Killer Dude the sledgehammer, and Killer Dude beat Ki with it until security dragged him away; Ki left on a stretcher. Commentary then called the bout a “No Contest”, but the page’s result line names Killer Dude the winner.

Refereed by Graham Poll: Slasher beat Side Order (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Slasher Dive (8:10). After the bell the Phenomenal Army (the Phenomenons, the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores, Max Queue and Speedy Linx) surrounded Slasher and pinned him to the mat while Eric Cameron declared him a “Prisoner of War” and threw custard pies in his face.

Tag team match refereed by Uriah Rennie, the Phenomenons’ first match as a reunited team: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led to the ring by Borrico Agujero) against the Hardcore Elements (Roadkill Grill and Overturned Car). Roadkill Grill’s Aztecan suplex left both his and Shane Stone’s shoulders on the mat and the referee counted three on both — “Both combatants have been pinned!” (11:24); commentary: “It’s called a draw.”

Johnny Walker against Keflon (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), refereed by Graham Poll. The Phenomenal Army (the Phenomenons Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, CHL #2 and CHL #3, Max Queue and Speedy Linx) paraded Keflon out as their newest member; Shane Stone slapped him on the back and Keflon fell down the ramp into the ring post and landed on his neck in the ring. Walker covered him: 1-2-3 (0:00:03). Eric Cameron then handed Walker Keflon’s helmet and the Army ran off with their new member.

Six-man tag team match refereed by Des Galpin between two Stable Wars entrants: Bluntman Inc. (the R.P.A. — Skull and Deck — and “Baby Psycho” Trent Lucas) against the Elements of Destruction (The Plague, “TNT” Tommy N Taylor — no iwf/giwf/uwf record — and Killer Dude, led by Evan McCann). The Outcastz (Jaxx, Blade and Slasher) broke it up, wheeled a bin to the ramp and threw all six men into it, then pushed it off the stage. No decision was announced.

The Dragoons (Eiji Kanatsu and Bahamut) defended the North American Tag Team Titles against the Bringers of Darkness (Venom and Onslaught, led by the Watcher), a rematch of the summer of 2000, refereed by Uriah Rennie. Eiji Kanatsu and Onslaught brawled outside to the ten count: “The verdict: A DOUBLE COUNTOUT !” The Dragoons kept the titles.

Refereed by Nelson Steel: “The Dart-Break Kid” Gary Clark (led by Simon Lyons) against the Intercontinental Champion Luca the Imp in LUCABOT (non-title on the schedule). The Circus of the Damned’s mimes and midgets ambushed LUCABOT and ejected Luca from the cockpit; Max Queue and LINKABOT, then the Phenomenons dropping from the rafters, tarred and feathered LUCABOT; Lady Luck hammered Luca, and Pete Steele and Ole Gus set LUCABOT alight. No decision was announced.

Refereed by Uriah Rennie: The Plague (led by Evan McCann) beat “The Definer Of Hardcore” Chomps — called “Chomps v2.0” in commentary, the son of the earlier Chomps — with the Black Death (6:20). Before the bell Killer Dude attacked Chomps in the parking lot, put him through a table and carried him to the ring.

GIWF Television Championship, refereed by Nelson Steel: “Baby Psycho” Trent Lucas (c) against “A.S.S.” Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third. Blade came over the guardrail with a sledgehammer; as Trent went to confront him on the apron, Saunders rolled Lucas up (12:36) — the new Television Champion. Blade then put Trent through the announce table and dragged him backstage.

Refereed by Nelson Steel: “Re-Run” Johnny Walker beat “pww killa” hardkore (no iwf/giwf/uwf record; led to the ring by gul’dan the hardkore penguin) when the referee stopped the fight in Walker’s Olympic Game (5:22). Commentary: Walker now calls joining the Phenomenons a mistake.

First blood match refereed by Isiah Heywood: Killer Dude beat “The Definer Of Hardcore” Chomps (“Chomps the 2nd” in commentary) when Chomps was busted open at ringside and the referee stopped the match on seeing the blood (41:59); the time limit expired mid-bout and the referee let it continue.

Refereed by Nelson Steel: Luca, piloting “LB” Lucabot, against Slasher, for Slasher’s killing of White Wolf. Luca came at Slasher with an axe and LUCABOT’s buzz saw until LUCABOT overrode him (“Directive Two”); after LUCABOT’s Escobomb Luca stood over the fallen Slasher with the axe raised, buried it in the mat instead, apologised to the fans and left the ring — the referee called a No Contest.

GIWF Television Championship: “A.S.S.” Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third (c) came out in a three-piece suit, handed Blade a sheet of paper and lay down on the ring apron; Blade dropped an elbow from the ring post and pinned him (0:05) — the new Television Champion. Commentary reads the papers as Saunders’s reward to Blade for helping him against Luca at Stable Wars.

Tag match refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero) against The Plague and “TNT” Tommy N Taylor (led by Evan McCann; Tommy N Taylor has no iwf/giwf/uwf record). The Plague pinned Eric Cameron with the Black Death (13:26).

GIWF World Tag Titles, refereed by Nelson Steel: Street Science (E Razor and Studog Escobar) against the champions, the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores (CHL#2 and CHL#3). E Razor made CHL#3 submit to the Razor’s Edge (14:52) and Street Science were announced the winners, but E Razor would not release the hold on CHL#2 and the referee reversed the decision: the Luchadores kept the titles by disqualification.

Main event, GIWF World Heavyweight Championship, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Prodigy (c) against Jay Phoenix. The Prodigy had hit the Coup de gras and had a two count when Gary Clark, Simon Lyons, Pete Steele, Ole’ Gus, Luca and LUCABOT — the UP YORS union — came out, named their demands and staged a sit-in in the ring. No decision was given.

Four corners match refereed by Graham Poll: “The Common Man” Ezra Kazee, back in the GIWF, beat three debutants — “J” J Woods, “Tie1on” Freddie Forever and “Ms. Perfectionist” Alice Carter (none has an iwf/giwf/uwf record) — making Freddie Forever submit to the Waling crab (10:06). The bout was worked with tags.

Falls count anywhere, refereed by Nelson Steel: Killer Dude beat “The Dean of Destruction” Disaster (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Killer Smash back in the ring (28:13), after a brawl through the arena, up and down its stairways and floors; the time limit expired and the referee let it continue.

Billed for the GIWF Television Championship, refereed by Nelson Steel: Blade (c) beat “TNT” Tommy N Taylor (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Cutting Edge (12:25). Before the bell Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third demanded “THE belt” back; Blade put him through the announce table, Oliver of the Academy took the belt, and TNT attacked Blade from behind as the bell rang. Commentary disputed whether the title was still on the line (“a non-title match” / “Saunders has no authority to strip anybody of any title”); Blade kept it.

Tag team match refereed by Graham Poll: Q-Factor (“Your Deep Blue Phenom” Max Queue-arollox and “Speedy Link” Link Anchorman, led to the ring by the Klue-Tang-Plan and Helix the Phenomenal Lost Boy) beat the Hardcore Elements (Overturned Car and “Meathead” Roadkill Grill) when Link Anchorman reversed Overturned Car’s cover (1:43) — Q-Factor’s first win.

Main event, GIWF World Heavyweight Championship in a steel cage, refereed by Graham Poll: Gurgles (c, led by Lady Luck) against Jay Phoenix, the “Winner of First Match” — Jay had beaten Benjita Kea in the opening match for the right. Both men moonsaulted from the cage; neither could rise by the referee’s ten, and the verdict was a draw (18:03), Gurgles keeping the title.

Gary Clark (led to the ring by Simon Lyons) against a “Mystery Opponent”, refereed by Isiah Heywood: the announcers joked that it was Luca, then Rosso, but it was Taff (Thirteen, the ring name he took in June 2000), with Zeta (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Clark hit the Retribution and the count had reached “One, two, thr…” when Curt Raines yanked the referee out of the ring and wrecked Clark’s knee with a steel chair; Taff and Zeta joined in. No decision was announced.

2-on-1 handicap match refereed by Isiah Heywood: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, the North American Tag Team Champions, led to the ring by Borrico Agujero) against Venom II (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), over his refusal to change his name. Shane Stone hit the Cyclone and the count had reached “One, two, thr…” when the lights flashed: a string-puppet “Luca”, then the Watcher and Strider of the Bringers of Darkness; Venom II fled. Venom and Onslaught attacked the Phenomenons and hanged both men from nooses before the Watcher had them let down. No decision was announced.

Curt Raines’s in-ring return, against a “Mystery Opponent” he had booked himself: “Hard Workin', American Built” Brian Morris (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Raines offered a handshake, jumped Morris from behind, and made him tap out to a Japanese leg roll into hiza-wakigatame, refereed by Graham Poll (0:0:24).

Opening tag match, refereed by Graham Poll: Corrupt Judgment (The Judge and The Jury) against the R.P.A (Skull and Deck), “the newest recruits of UP YORS”. Skull and Deck were still brawling with The Judge on the floor at the referee’s ten: a double countout (the verdict), recorded as a draw.

THC Title, refereed by Uriah Rennie, made when Lyle Wile and Chris Cage could not appear: “LB” Lucabot (Luca the Imp in L.U.C.A.B.O.T.) against the champion Brad Stratus. Stratus submitted to the Pneumatic Nut Crush (14:44) and Luca became THC Champion.

Main event, refereed by Graham Poll: Gurgles (the World Champion), Adam Finn (Hybrid) and Jay Phoenix, led by Lady Luck, against the Nu-Outcastz — Blade, “The Eternal Flame” Brad Johnson and the Plague, led by Evan McCann. Gurgles held Brad Johnson in the Big Top until the referee stopped the fight (28:36). Afterwards UP YORS (Gary Clark, LUCABOT, TNT and Luca) attacked the Outcastz; LUCABOT harpooned Jay Phoenix as he walked away, dragged him back and tied him to a turnbuckle while Luca berated him; Lady Luck offered him her hand.

Billed as the R.P.A (Skull and Deck) against the Phenomenons (led by Borrico Agujero), a tag match refereed by Isiah Heywood. When the Bringers of Darkness came to the ring, “Shane Stone” pulled off a near-perfect mask to reveal Max Queue, and “Eric Cameron” was Link Anchorman — Q-Factor had wrestled in the Phenomenons’ place. The real Shane Stone rode in on the Phenomenal Elephants with the Phenomenal Army and chased the Bringers of Darkness out of the arena. The match did not end; no decision was given.

Refereed by Isiah Heywood: Jay Phoenix against “A.S.S.” Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third. Taff, dressed as a Lucalike, came out on a donkey (“LUCAZADE”) to taunt Jay; while Saunders stood reading a book in a neutral corner, Jay Phoenix crept up and rolled him up with an inside cradle for the win (7:41).

Billed as a six-man (“Trent Lucas + 2 Partners -v- RPA & Partner”); neither side found partners, so it was made a handicap match, refereed by Graham Poll: the RPA (Skull and Deck) beat Trent Lucas when Skull hit the Red Elbow and pinned him (14:57).

North American Championship (Punishment’s) and Intercontinental Championship (Jaxx’s) both on the line, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Punishment’s clothesline felled the referee; Adam Finn came to ringside with a chair aimed at Jaxx, but Jaxx turned Punishment into it, and Jaxx pinned Punishment once the referee was revived (21:18), holding both titles.
Refereed by Uriah Rennie: Toxic Shock lost to “TNT” Tommy N Taylor (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), pinned after the Big Boom (9:26).

Refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Dragoons (Eiji Kanatsu and Bahamut) beat Q-Factor (Max Queue, billed “Max Queue-arollox”, and Link Anchorman; led out by the Klue-Tang-Plan and Helix the Phenomenal Lost Boy) and the Bringers of Darkness (Venom and Onslaught, led out by the Watcher) when Bahamut pinned Venom after the Dragon Bomb (18:29).
Refereed by Graham Poll: Lee Coulter and the debuting Ian Wynn (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) fought to a double countout (“The verdict: A DOUBLE COUNTOUT !”); Coulter attacked Wynn before the bell.

Tag team match refereed by Nelson Steel: the Hardcore Elements (Roadkill Grill and Overturned Car) beat the debuting Destruction (Whirlwind Wilmott and Hurricane Hurst; no iwf/giwf/uwf records) when Roadkill Grill pinned Wilmott after the Roadkill Cafe (7:16).
Refereed by Graham Poll. White Wolf beat "Coldfire" Zach Shook, whose first pay-per-view it was, with the Artic Splash (7:50); Shook complained about a fast count.
Studog Escobar, led to the ring by John Barnes, beat Inferno ("Fighting out of Boston, Mass... Weighing in at 210 pounds..."; no GIWF record) by submission to the Final Buck Submission move (0:37).

Team Esco (John Barnes and Henrique Escobar) defended the World Tag-Team Titles against the Phenomenons, led to the ring by Borrico Agujero. The Phenomenons won by disqualification (3:05) when the Mighty Israelites drove a golf buggy down the ramp, ran over Eric Cameron and stole Team Esco's Diamond Ducat of Dorking; the titles did not change hands on a disqualification.

Main event, for the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship, refereed by Paul Alcock. Lew Spectre, led to the ring by Richard Ray Vaughn, worked the champion over with the Figure-Four Sleeper, the Ankle Lock and the Reverse Cradle Piledriver and threw the referee into the corner three times; Vaughn tripped McGrubber, pulled down the top rope and hit him with the briefcase. The time limit expired and the referee let the match continue; Hamish McGrubber retained with the Highland Fling (26:19). Afterwards D Dawg Benny-J and Luca attacked Spectre, D Dawg driving a chair onto his knee and an iron bucket into his head; the Phenomenons ran out and brawled with the Mitchell Brothers, and The Bum Boozler's crew handcuffed Spectre to the ropes.

Non-title tag match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the New Renegades (Gary Clark and Justin Arnold) against Natural Terror (Craig Jericho and Chris Jarvie; no GIWF record). Gary Clark attacked Craig Jericho before the bell and pinned Chris Jarvie with the Retribution (8:15).

The "Millennium Million Midget March Match" (the commentators' name for it; the fed's own line calls it only "a tag team match"), refereed by Mike Reed: the Phenomenons, Commissioners of the Tag Team Division, led by Borrico Agujero and representing Senor Mime, against “Naitch” Taff (Thirteen, under the ring name he took in June 2000) and Killer Dude, led by Zeta and representing her. Beside the fight, each team had to tag four midgets in Dragoons' Fan Club T-shirts among the crowd of midgets at ringside, and the losing team's patron would leave the GIWF. Mid-match two newcomers, Dean Banks and TJ Morgan, appeared, powerbombed Taff and Killer Dude, revealed Star Trek uniforms and brawled with the Phenomenons, locking Shane Stone in a camel clutch and Boston crab until Eric Cameron drove them off with a steel cane; meanwhile Taff tagged the last of the four midgets, and Taff and Killer Dude were declared the winners (15:12), so Senor Mime left the GIWF.

For the GIWF North American Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Graham Poll: the champions, the Dark Lords (Gabriel and Evil, led by Luca), against Apocalypse (Richard Gordon and Steven Fredericks, led by Dave 'The Chain' Roberts; no GIWF record). Evil attacked Richard Gordon before the bell. Mid-match the Dragoons (Tiamat and Bahamut) came to the ring and Bahamut chokeslammed the referee; the Dark Lords left the ring and the Dragoons beat Apocalypse down with steel chairs and the Dragon Fall. No decision was given.

The Television Champion's first defence, refereed by Nelson Steel; billed as Inferno ("Fighting out of Death Valley, Texas..."). The time limit expired and the referee let the match continue; Inferno retained, pinning White Wolf with the Meltdown (23:08), and White Wolf complained about a fast count.

Main event, for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, with Ben Jackson as special referee: the champion, the Shark, against Lew Spectre, led by Richard Ray Vaughn. Before the bell Jackson, as "Eye Candy" Ben Jericho, announced that the winner would face him at the next pay-per-view. Vaughn distracted the Shark and hit him with the briefcase again and again; Lew Spectre won the title after 1:13:53, when the Shark passed out in the Figure-Four Sleeper. Afterwards the Firestarter returned and went after Spectre; Lyle Wile, Deke Aurora and the Prodigy laid out the Firestarter and the Shark, Spectre tore up Jackson's contract, and the four stood together with Spectre's World title and Aurora's North American and Intercontinental titles.
