matches.note: Brad Stratus, led to the ring by Rayna, against Garry Maximum (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), their feud carried over from TCW; Garry Maximum won by escaping the cage through the door (11:30).

The World and North American Tag Team Titles unified, refereed by Graham Poll: Street Science (E Razor and Studog Escobar), the World Tag Champions, against the North American Tag Champions, the Phenomenons (Eric Cameron and Shane Stone, led to the ring by Borrico Agujero); the third team billed, the Bringers of Darkness, did not come out. As Studog Escobar set up the Nuclear Mega-Ton Escobomb the lights went out, and Venom and Onslaught ran in with golden chairs, knocked the referee out and laid out Shane Stone and Eric Cameron; Studog Escobar handed Strider a briefcase from under the ring (the commentators took it for a pay-off), revived the referee and pinned Eric Cameron. Street Science became the Unified Tag Team Champions (15:46).

For the THC Title, no disqualification and no countout, refereed by Isiah Heywood, under the stipulation that the loser takes the title: Luca, who wanted rid of the belt, in LUCABOT (c), against Alexander Venom (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), led to the ring by Jenny. Blade had tampered with LUCABOT backstage; it would not pin Venom and broke down, and Blade and Jaxx attacked Venom and dragged him onto LUCABOT for the three count. Alexander Venom won (18:03), and Luca stayed THC Champion.
For the GIWF Intercontinental Championship, refereed by Isiah Heywood: Jaxx (c) pinned Adam “Hybrid” Finn with the Jaxxhammer and retained (13:22).

For the GIWF North American Championship, under THC rules, refereed by Graham Poll: Cpl. Punishment (c) attacked Slasher before the bell and, after an hour-long brawl through the arena, made him submit to the Lethal Injection (1:00:01).

Main event, for the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship, refereed by Graham Poll: Gurgles (c), led to the ring by Lady Luck, against Jay Phoenix. Jay Phoenix hit the Meltdown four times; Lady Luck tripped him twice and hit him with a chair, and Gurgles retained when Jay Phoenix submitted to a third straight Big Top (28:30).
Opening match, refereed by Nelson Steel: a rematch of CA$H’s low-blow win over Chomps. Chomps, still looking for his first GIWF win, pinned CA$H after a low blow of his own (9:14).

Triangle match, refereed by Nelson Steel: Cpl. Punishment against Scott Ross and “Crash” Alex Smith, led to the ring by Ole Jim (neither Ross nor Smith has an iwf/giwf/uwf record). Alex Smith pinned Cpl. Punishment after a third Crash & Burn (17:10); the commentators spoke of Smith as Pete Steele under another name, “allegedly”.

matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere/No-DQ/No-Countout/Last Man Standing match

matches.note: Main event, for the GIWF North American (“Native American”) Title, refereed by Mike Reed, foreign objects banned. The man introduced as Inferno was unmasked as Gay Phoenix, Luca’s dancer, after Jay Phoenix ran in from the back and knocked Lucabot into the burial plot; Lucabot winched itself out, and after a long fight Lucabot buried Jay Phoenix and won (22:35), Luca becoming North American Champion. On 7 January 2001 Jay Phoenix announced that the board had ruled Lucabot a foreign object and the title change invalid (giwf-suicide-2001-01-07).

Heaven & Hell match (Angel’s own creation; the only way to win was to strap the opponent to the symbol): Angel against Devils Disciple (led by The Gremlin). Mr. Meaner jumped Angel with a metal bar before the bell; Devils Disciple strapped Angel to the symbol and raised it (10:14).

For the GIWF North American Tag-Titles, refereed by Graham Barlow: the champions Tropical Storm (Miguel Lanza and Jamie Dermott) against the Shades of Hell (Damien and Wolf X, led by Destructive Everything; no iwf/giwf/uwf record), with Destructive Everything to serve Tropical Storm as their “maid” for seven days if the champions retained. Miguel Lanza pinned Wolf X after the Reef Dive Driver; Tropical Storm retained (12:25).

For the GIWF Intercontinental Championship, refereed by Graham Poll: Cpl. Punishment’s scheduled opponent Ueshiba Kancho withdrew (throat cancer) and the Corporal faced a mystery opponent billed “The Masked Man Number 3”, who came out to Joseph Rosso’s music in his ring attire. The masked man won the title when the referee stopped the match on the Flatliner Leg-Lock (12:56). The next card’s broadcast names him as Ben Jackson (“Jacksons late substitution as a mystery wrestler at Halloween Hell”, Sunday Afternoon Suicide 21 Nov 1999), and the fed’s own Intercontinental title history gives the reign to Ben Jackson.

Main event, first leg of the Gauntlet Match for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, refereed by Graham Poll: the champion Twiztid ran the gauntlet of the Youngbloods and Lew Spectre (a man who beat Twiztid would have to finish the gauntlet in his place). Eric Cameron hit the Showstopper and a 450 splash but Twiztid rolled him up with a small package (5:15).

Second leg of the Gauntlet Match for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, refereed by Mike Reed: Shane Stone (the commentators: “still is the longest serving Intercontinental Champion in GIWF History”) against the champion Twiztid, who pinned him with the Tilt-a-whirl powerbomb (8:26).

Third leg of the Gauntlet Match for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, refereed by Uriah Rennie: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against the champion Twiztid. Twiztid survived the Figure-Four Sleeper; the time limit expired but the referee let the match continue, and Twiztid pinned Spectre after a top-rope Splash Mountain while Spectre complained of a fast count (20:49).

Final leg of the Gauntlet Match for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, refereed by Graham Poll: Lyle Wile hit the ring early; Twiztid won with a flipped powerbomb and the pin while Wile complained of a fast count (11:24), then burned Wile’s face with Cpl. Punishment’s cattle prod.

Table ladder tag match: Misled Youth (Freak and Jack Manson; Jack Manson has no iwf/giwf/uwf record) against Gangster Power (Franky Devlan and Nails Zanetti, led by “Chicago” Mike; no record). Two trench-coated men at ringside froze Gangster Power; Freak put Franky Devlan through a table with a swinging bulldog and Misled Youth won (7:18). Gangster Power left with the two men.

Best of three falls: “The Beautiful One” Daneel McCord (with Paula Thompson) against “Superstar” Ace Thunder (with Kitten) — if McCord won he got Kitten for the night, if Thunder won Kitten got Paula. Thunder took the first fall with the Thunderclap (0:32), McCord the second with the Sweetness Piledriver (4:53), Thunder the third with the Thunderclap (5:19).

For the GIWF Tag-Team Titles: the champions Team Esco (“The Greatest Footballer Alive” John Barnes and “110%” Henrique Escobar) against the Cossack Warriors (Ivan and Yuri Kickabollockov, led by “The Mad Monk” Rasputin; no iwf/giwf/uwf record), who fought to see Anastasia. Barnes pinned Ivan with the Atomic Barnestormer; Team Esco retained (8:06). Armageddon attacked the champions afterwards and Studog Escobar and E Razor made the save.

Four corners match for the GIWF North American Title and the GIWF World Television Title (the first man pinned was to lose the TV title; the North American Title went to the last man standing): the North American Champion Cockney Rebel, the Television Champion “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn), Studog Escobar (led by John Barnes) and “The Executioner” David Rico (led by David Head). Rebel, Rico and Studog all pinned Spectre together at 1:14 (“The winner is ???????”; the commentators called him screwed out of the match); Studog then pinned Rico with the Nuclear Escobomb (6:29), and the Rebel pinned Studog with the Last Orders to retain the North American Title (11:36). The fed left the TV title undecided on the night; its title history keeps Lew Spectre champion until 3 July 1999 (giwf-television-r007).

Main event for the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship, in Portree: the champion “The Highlander” Hamish McGrubber against “Bobby Brian Bangemhard” the Bum Boozler (led by Gimp). The time limit expired and the referee let the match continue; McGrubber submitted to the Bum Booz Bugger after 122 seconds and the Bum Boozler won the title (23:08).

matches.stipulation: Television Title Battle Royal (Winner gets TV Title Shot)
matches.note: Over-the-top battle royal of eight: Inferno, Jayson Fury, Lithium, Cypher, Taff, Jaxx, Ezra Kazee and Angel (Fury, Lithium and Cypher have no GIWF record; Taff is Thirteen under his new ring name). The Dark Lords came to the ring mid-match and Evil threw out Lithium, Ezra Kazee, Angel, Taff and Cypher; Inferno, in his debut, hit Evil with a low blow to save Jaxx and Jayson Fury and then left over the top rope himself; Evil pressed Fury out and Gabriel chokeslammed Jaxx over the top, and Jaxx, the last entrant standing, was ruled the winner of the TV title shot.

Triple threat, refereed by Mike Reid: Pogo, Murda U (formerly B-Z; no GIWF record) and Luca. Pogo swung Luca like a baseball bat into Murda U, hit the Innovator of Violence, threw Luca on top of Murda U and pinned him (13:08); the fed declared both Pogo and Luca the winners. Ben Jackson, as Suicide Anglo, raised both men's hands afterwards.

For the GIWF North American Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the champions, the Bringers of Darkness (Venom and Onslaught, led by The Watcher), against the Vallhallans (Vespasien and Angelus, led by Sophia), in their first pay-per-view. Vespasien and Onslaught fought on the floor and both teams were counted out.
The first bout on a GIWF pay-per-view: Lew Spectre, led by Richard Ray Vaughn, made Alien submit to an elbow submission (9:32).

Attitude Adjustment (Ian Ice and Mike Diamond) against a mystery team, revealed as “Pretty in the City”: Daneel McCord and The Golden Drifter in their debut as a team. McCord pinned Ian Ice with the Sweetness Piledriver (13:22).

Every singles wrestler without a singles match that night; the winner earned a Television Title shot on Tuesday Night Global. Also in it: the Paid Assassin and The Assassin (of the Mutha Buckers), neither with a GIWF record (labels in eliminations). “Jason Parson” is the billing of the lineage’s jazon-parzon. The Grim Reaper won (18:17) after, the commentary says, cracking the Paid Assassin with his Skull Staff.

For the GIWF Intercontinental Championship; Lew Spectre in Stone’s corner. The Golden Drifter dragged Spectre to the back, the Grim Reaper threw Stone a baseball bat, a masked man (unmasked by Black Dragon as Studog Escobar) hit the Reaper; the Reaper finally hit Cockney Rebel with a chair and Steven Lodge called for the DQ — Cockney Rebel won by disqualification (11:29) and Stone kept the title. Earlier Stone and Spectre had handcuffed The Guv’nor and Hamish McGrubber in their locker room.

Billed as a Man -v- Beast match. White Wolf threw Luca out of the ring and into the crowd; Evil then laid White Wolf out with his gauntlet and the Damnation. The page prints no result line; the commentary calls it “a win for White Wolf”.
For the GIWF World Television Title. Lew Spectre came to ringside and speared Coma through the ropes as he went for the ladder, and Ozzy Douglas retrieved the title (17:02).
For the GIWF World Championship, Jason Parson the special referee: Curt Raines won the title (23:21).

matches.note: Refereed by Nelson Steel: the Firestarter beat “The Odd” Hardcore Oddy (led by Jess) by pinfall after hitting him with his own guitar (8:58), winning the week with Jess; Oddy’s contract would have made him number one contender for the Television Title. (“Inferno” is the Firestarter’s finishing move.)

For the GIWF North American Tag Team Titles, refereed by Uriah Rennie, the fifth of the Phenomenons -v- Dragoons series: the champions drove the GIWF PPV Promotion Garbage Truck to the ring. “Suave” Stevie West handcuffed Eiji Kanatsu to the guardrail, and Shane Stone and Eric Cameron hit Bahamut with the Phenomenal Ending for the pin; the Phenomenons retained (23:37).
Refereed by Mike Reed, on Joseph Rosso’s “Night of No Disqualification”: the Prodigy (led by Miss Pain) beat the returning Fagen Gilchrist when Miss Pain’s low blow set up the End (13:45).

For the GIWF Intercontinental Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: Lyle Wile (the champion of record) against Mr. Meaner (Ezra Kazee), who had surrendered the belt he had taken as “Sesom” earlier in the day. Wile won with the Facelift (11:38); Meaner handed him the belt and left.

For the GIWF World Tag Team Titles, refereed by Graham Poll: Law & Order (Studog Escobar and Cpl. Punishment) against the “New” Youngbloods (Lew Spectre and Lyle Wile, led by Richard Ray Vaughn). Studog wrestled the whole match; when he finally reached for the tag, Cpl. Punishment pulled his hand away and hit him with the cattle prod, and Lyle Wile pinned him after the Facelift (21:50). Spectre revealed the Corporal had never left the Youngbloods, and Richard Ray Vaughn presented three World Tag Team belts to Spectre, Wile and the Corporal.

Refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Masked Man, led to the ring by Pete Steele, beat Curt Raines with the Crash N’ Burn in the middle of a ring Pete Steele had set alight (13:13); the commentators take this as proof that Pete Steele is not the man under the mask. Steele then set Raines on fire before the firefighters put him out.

Tag match, refereed by Graham Poll: “Tornado” Shane Stone and Bob the Robot against “Main Event” Eric Cameron and “Asso” Borrico Agujero, meant to settle the Phenomenons’ break-up. Stone begged Cameron’s forgiveness and the two embraced, then shouted “APRIL FOOLS!” and went back to fighting; Cameron pulled out Bob the Robot’s power cord and Stone drove Bob out of the arena on a forklift. The match was ruled a no contest (24:13).

matches.stipulation: No Disqualification and Last Man Standing rules in the Cell
matches.note: The Hall of Fame Grudge Match, refereed by Graham Poll, with Richard Ray Vaughn banned from ringside by Lew Spectre’s own stipulations: Lew Spectre’s GIWF career against Al Crud’s mother becoming Spectre’s domestic servant. Spectre attacked Crud on the ramp before the bell; after a long fight in and around the Cell, Al Crud hit the Mother Crudder and Spectre, lying in the wreckage of a table, did not answer the referee’s ten count. Al Crud won, and Lew Spectre’s GIWF career was over.

Main event, for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Luca in L.U.C.A.B.O.T. (champion) against Pete Steele, led to the ring by Ole Gus. With the referee knocked down, Celest attacked Steele and LUCABOT with a crowbar; a figure in the Crimson Ghost’s cloak dropped from the rafters, tied Steele in the ropes and unmasked as Jay Phoenix, whose ambulance departure earlier in the night had been staged. The brothers pulled Luca from the machine and destroyed LUCABOT with a virus disk. No decision was announced; Luca kept the title.

Opening triangle match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: The Plague (a late replacement for his THC Title shot at Gurgles) against Craig Wright and Max Damage. Craig Wright and Max Damage brawled outside until the referee’s count of ten — the verdict a double countout, with no winner declared. The Forces of Darkness (“The Reaper” Jared Crafter and Riggs) then attacked Max Damage and the other Reaper.

Refereed by Graham Poll: “ICK” Ice Cold Killa against “Baby Psycho” Trent Lucas. Each man laid out the referee (the Killa Smash, the Spotlight); after simultaneous chair shots neither beat the count — the verdict a double countout.

Main event for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, refereed by Uriah Rennie: L.U.C.A.B.O.T. (c; Luca the Imp’s robot) against Al Crud. Pete Steele brought Al a can of beer mid-match; when Lew Spectre walked out onto the ramp with the Intercontinental title, Crud turned to him and L.U.C.A.B.O.T. struck from behind — Al Crud submitted to the Pneumatic Nut Crush (29:22).

Number-one contenders’ match for the North American Tag-Team titles: the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey) against the Fan-Tastics (Stalker and Obsessed, led by Hyper Girl), the Rylance Ladz (Dan and Chris Rylance) and Shades of Hell (Damien and Wolf X); the Rylance Ladz and Shades of Hell have no iwf/giwf/uwf record. Eriu pinned Wolf X after the Kissing the Blarney Stone; the Fomorians won (7:35).

Number-one contender’s match for the GIWF Television Title: “Superstar” Stevie May against Jack Leer, Angel (“From Rio de Janeiro, Brazil… 300 pounds”, in his debut) and Josh Dillinger (Jack Leer and Josh Dillinger have no iwf/giwf/uwf record). May made Leer submit to the Showstoppa, Angel pinned May with the Front face Pancake, and Dillinger pinned Angel after the Leon-Tamer Moonsault. Josh Dillinger won (12:24).

Final of the tournament for the first GIWF North American Tag-Titles: Tropical Storm (Miguel Lanza and Jaime Dermont) against RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ), with the commentator Toby Jenkins as special referee. Dermont poked Triple J in the chest — “the finger of Doom” — and pinned him (0:41); Tropical Storm became the first North American Tag-Team champions.

For the GIWF World Tag-Team Championships: the champions the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero) against “The Fallen One” Nephilim and “The Canadian Luchadore” Deke Aurora (led by Angelique). RIMJOB came to ringside; Triple J argued with Stone while Aurora and Nephilim double-teamed Cameron and J. Harold Christ hit him with a backdrop driver off the top turnbuckle. Nephilim pinned Cameron: Nephilim and Deke Aurora won the titles (9:18).

Main event, for the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship: the champion “The Undead Walker” David Rico (led by David Head) against “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against Twiztid. Lyle Wile, not scheduled, joined the commentary and left his seat to hit Twiztid with a steel chair and the Face Lift at ringside; Vaughn’s briefcase shots went both ways; Spectre tagged Twiztid in and Twiztid pinned Rico with the Tilt-a-whirl powerbomb. Twiztid won the title (19:30); afterwards the Keeper proclaimed the Order of the Hammer.

Tag match: Team Esco (“110%” Henrique Escobar and “The Greatest Footballer Alive” John Barnes) against RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ), who had eliminated Team Esco from the tag-title tournament. Triple J submitted to Barnes’s Time Warp; Team Esco won (10:47).

For the GIWF North American Title, a cage match with David Rico as special guest referee: the champion Cockney Rebel against “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre. Rico sat on Spectre while the Rebel escaped the cage (11:50). The Rebel then announced he was leaving for the BWF and offered Spectre the belt — only to smash it into his face; he and the Guv’nor beat down Spectre and Richard Ray Vaughn, the Phenomenons were held back by security, and the Rebel left by helicopter. The commentators called Spectre the new North American title holder.

A ladder match for Hamish McGrubber’s release from his contract, with Al Crud as special guest referee, billed as “Hamish McGrubber -v- Rob Williams”. Rob Williams never came out; Lew Spectre, with Cecil Worthington and Richard Ray Vaughn, took his place as the North American champion. Spectre pulled down the contract, but it fell into Crud’s hands and the match went on; Crud refused to stop it on Spectre’s Figure Four Sleeper and McGrubber pinned Spectre after the Highland Fling (8:12). McGrubber tore up the contract.

The final of the tournament for the vacant GIWF World Tag-Titles, a triangle match (no eliminations; the first fall decides): the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero), the Brotherhood (Phoenix and Raven) and Underground (Abdul Rahaman and Da Heat, led by Carl Big). While the Fomorians attacked Carl Big, Eric Cameron pinned Da Heat with the Showstopper; the Phenomenons won the World Tag-Titles (16:53), and “every one of the Youngbloods has a belt”. The Brotherhood then left the GIWF.

Main event for the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship: the champion Studog Escobar (led by John Barnes) against “The Executioner” David Rico (led by David Head). Barnes’s chair shot missed Rico and hit Studog; Rico pinned Studog with the Execution and won the title (18:26).

Benito Cavalera, led by Leanne Hatchett, against The Preacher (of the Hatchett family; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) in the first “Buried in the Thunderdome” match, won by burying the opponent in one of two graves inside the Thunderdome. Celest, believed dead, rose from the first grave and attacked Cavalera; Ace Thunder rose from the second, laid Celest out, and he and Cavalera buried Celest and the Preacher — the referee called for the bell (27:41).

GIWF World Tag-Team Title match, refereed by Nelson Steel: the champions the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by The Punisher, Borrico Agujero and “Suave” Stevie West) beat the R.P.A (Skull and Deck), Eric Cameron pinning Deck with the Showstopper (16:49).

Main event for the GIWF World Heavyweight Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: Al Crud (c) against Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn), L.U.C.A.B.O.T. and Jay Phoenix. Jay Phoenix submitted to L.U.C.A.B.O.T.’s Pneumatic Nut Crush (26:30); L.U.C.A.B.O.T. — Luca the Imp’s robot, filed under luca-the-imp — is the new champion.

Spectre eliminated Barnes and Pyro and was then pinned by a fresh Al Crud.
Stable Wars round two (c): Curt Raines pinned Hamish McGrubber with the Rainedrop DDT (12:55); the Youngbloods’ pair advanced to the final.

The 1999 GIWF Stable Wars final, Big John McCarthy the special referee: Curt Raines rolled Pete Steele up and both men’s shoulders were down for the three; the fed ruled both pinned, no champions were crowned and McCarthy pulled the four out of the ring.

notes: Unlisted bout: The Grim Reaper beat Brimstone (no GIWF record) (5:02).

matches.note: Stable Wars 2000 quarter-final, tag team match, refereed by Nelson Steel: "Crash" Pete Steele and The Masked Man (led to the ring by Ole Gus and Speaker) against Nephilim and Celest. The card bills the Order's side as "Nephilim & RiVeN"; Nephilim brings Celest out as the Order of the Hammer's latest inductee and Celest takes the ring, with Chris Hatchet coming down as the Order's "manager for the evening". Nephilim and Celest won when Nephilim pinned The Masked Man after the Spiked Celestial Lights Brainbuster (10:58) and met Lew Spectre and Lyle Wile in the semi-final (matches[4]).

Stable Wars 2000 quarter-final, tag team match, refereed by Graham Poll: the New Youngbloods, “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre and “The Stylemeister” Lyle Wile (led to the ring by Richard Ray Vaughn and Miss Pain), beat Studog and Henrique Escobar (Law & Order) when Lew Spectre’s Figure-Four Sleeper made Henrique Escobar submit (11:56). The side names the unit as the fed billed it and the two members who wrestled; the pair lost the semi-final to Nephilim and Celest (matches[4]).

Stable Wars 2000 quarter-final, tag team match, refereed by Nelson Steel: the Youngbloods’ second team, the Widowmaker and the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadore — who unmasked before the bell as the Prodigy, “the final member of The Youngblood team” — against Al Crud and Gurgles (the Stable with no name, led by Lady Luck). The Prodigy refused every tag and walked out, and the Widowmaker submitted to Gurgles’ Big Top (9:06).
