matches.note: Stable Wars III, first round: Krushin Time (Krush, Kilo Jones and L.U.C.A.B.O.T.) against the faux-Youngbloods (billed “Youngbloods v3.0”: Benjita Kea, Studog Escobar, Lyle Wile and Hybrid). Krush turned on his own team, handing Benjita Kea a screwdriver that Kea drove into L.U.C.A.B.O.T.’s circuit board before pinning him (13:42).

Stable Wars III, first round: the Forces of Darkness (Jared Crafter, Riggs, Mike Montgomery and Konrad Karter) against the Outcastz, whom they had attacked backstage before the show; without Luca, the Outcastz won when Jaxx got the pin (12:36). Riggs has no iwf/giwf/uwf record.

Stable Wars III, second round: Gurgles’ Circus of the Damned (Gurgles, Pete Steele, Gary Clark and Señor Mime) against the faux-Youngbloods (billed “Youngbloods v3.0”: Benjita Kea, Studog Escobar, Lyle Wile and Hybrid). Pete Steele and Lyle Wile were both counted out; Studog Escobar then pinned Señor Mime, and the faux-Youngbloods went through (18:55). Señor Mime has no iwf/giwf/uwf record.

Stable Wars III, semi-final: the Outcastz (Jaxx, Slasher and L.U.C.A.B.O.T.) against the faux-Youngbloods (billed “Youngbloods v3.0”: Benjita Kea, Studog Escobar, Lyle Wile and Hybrid). With one fall left, Jaxx refused Luca’s tag and walked away, and Studog Escobar rolled up L.U.C.A.B.O.T. (13:13) — the Outcastz, Krushin Time and Alexander Sebastian Saunders had all planned to cost Luca the tournament.

matches.stipulation: Stable Wars III Grand Final match
matches.note: Stable Wars III Grand Final, elimination rules: P.EP Inc. (The Prodigy, Al Crud, Cpl. Punishment and Jay Phoenix) against the faux-Youngbloods (billed “Youngbloods v3.0”: Benjita Kea, Studog Escobar, Lyle Wile and Hybrid). Kea, Al Crud and The Prodigy went early; Hybrid pinned Jay Phoenix with the Exclamation Mark; Cpl. Punishment then eliminated Lyle Wile and Hybrid alone before Studog Escobar pinned him after four Nuclear Mega-Ton Escobombs (56:53). The faux-Youngbloods won Stable Wars III.

Stable Wars III, first round: the Phenomenal Army (led by the Phenomenons, Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, with Max Queue and CHL #2) against Bluntman Inc. (Trent Lucas, Skull and Deck). Eric Cameron pinned Trent Lucas with the Showstopper (16:15). CHL #2 has no iwf/giwf/uwf record of his own.

Stable Wars III, second round (two eliminations to lose): the Phenomenal Army against P.EP Inc. (The Prodigy, Al Crud, Cpl. Punishment and Jay Phoenix). Shane Stone eliminated Al Crud with the Cyclone; Cpl. Punishment made CHL #2 submit; Jay Phoenix pinned Max Queue with the Meltdown to put P.EP Inc. through (16:32).

Stable Wars III Redemption Round, sudden death: the Circus of the Damned (Gurgles, Pete Steele and Gary Clark, joined by the Crimson Ghost after Señor Mime was taken out backstage), the Phenomenal Army and the 4T3W’s (Venom, Onslaught, L.U.C.A.B.O.T. and Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third). Shane Stone and Eric Cameron hit the Phenomenal Ending on Pete Steele but could not keep him down; Saunders sabotaged L.U.C.A.B.O.T. by remote and the Crimson Ghost pinned it (9:44). The Crimson Ghost and Señor Mime have no iwf/giwf/uwf record.

Stable Wars III, semi-final: the Circus of the Damned (Gurgles, Pete Steele and Gary Clark, with the Crimson Ghost) against P.EP Inc. Gurgles eliminated The Prodigy; Cpl. Punishment made Gurgles submit; Jay Phoenix pinned Gary Clark with the Meltdown (26:57).

name: IYC: Style and Substances

matches.note: The Phenomenons (led by Borrico Agujero, The Punisher and “Suave” Stevie West) v. the Serial Thrillers v. “Rock Hot” Joe Kenny and his mystery partner, Benito Cavalera, unveiled as the newest member of the Rebel Generation: Gabriel Talbot pinned Eric Cameron with the Stimulator (15:53).

Before the show the Spettro Di Avversione Mafia unmasked as Corporal Punishment, Scott Ross and Slasher, Hybrid’s red-cloaked ally as the World Champion Lyle Wile, and the Canadian Clique (with Julia Finn’s bat) beat Lew Spectre down. In the match Spectre, led by Richard Ray Vaughn, scored the first pin but Adam “Hybrid” Finn kept him down for the ten count after the Exclamation Mark (34:06).

For Luca’s North American Title: Luca, piloting LUCABOT (billed “Lucabot”, luca-the-imp’s aka), pinned Snake Phoenix with the Double-Implant DDT (22:50). The commentary says Snake Phoenix is not related to Jay Phoenix.

notes: Unlisted bout: Mesmerised (Henry and James; no GIWF record) beat Too Smutty (Silicone Trish and The Muffmaster) when Henry made Silicone Trish submit to the Armbreaker (11:14).

matches.note: For the GIWF World Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Neil Scott: the Dark Lords (billed as Evil and “The Fallen Angel” Gabrielle) in their first defence against Attitude Adjustment (Mike Diamond and Ian Ice) and Armageddon (“Motown” Don Carson and “Silver King” Kendall Stripp). Attitude Adjustment and Armageddon brawled outside and were both counted out; the fed declared the Dark Lords the winners (13:27).

Main event, refereed by Steven Lodge: Shane Stone (the Intercontinental Champion, with the chance to unify the titles) against the North American Champion Al Crud, only Crud’s title at stake. The Bum Boozler, at ringside for Stone, threw him a fire extinguisher and later broke up Crud’s pin after the Mother Crudder; the referee called for the DQ and Al Crud was the winner (11:12). Afterwards a masked man, Alien, laid Stone out with a chair and sent a challenge through him to Lew Spectre; Curt Raines and Jason Parson brawled into the ring.
Cockney Rebel’s GIWF debut (billed “Cokney Rebel”, fighting out of London): he pinned Daneel McCord with the Last Orders (5:18).
Time-limit draw: the bell rang as both men went down to a double clothesline; Daneel McCord had tripped the Boozler from ringside throughout.
The Dreamwarriors (billed John Constantine and Sandman) beat Armageddon (“Motown” Don Carson and “Silver King” Kendall Stripp) when Kendall Stripp submitted to Sandman’s torture rack (14:04).
The Dark Lords (Evil and Gabrielle, with Luca measuring a line seven inches from the ring) beat AmWt (Jack and Shawn): Evil pinned Shawn with the Damnation (10:31).

name: GIWF Suicide — 20 Mar 1999

matches.note: For the number-one contendership to the Dark Lords’ tag titles at March Maelstrom: the Dreamwarriors beat AmWt when the referee stopped it with Shawn unable to answer in Sandman’s Dreamweaver (7:30). Lew Spectre then came from under the ring and hit John Constantine with a chair.
A non-title bout with the North American champion Al Crud: both men were counted out (a double countout).
Peter Steele (billed “Pete Steel”, led by Ole Gus) pinned E Razor with the Crash & Burn (9:06); The Assassin, Studog Escobar and E Razor then beat him down and spike-piledrove him onto a chair.

Elimination rules, for the shot at Shane Stone’s Intercontinental title at March Maelstrom: the Grim Reaper pinned White Wolf; a masked man’s DDT left the Reaper counted out and Cockney Rebel won (8:06). Shane Stone, who had phoned in claiming to be on a plane, then ran in and beat Rebel down with a chair.

notes: Unlisted bout: Studog Escobar (led by John Barnes) pinned his stablemate The Assassin (“Big Ed, The Ruthless Bastard”, led by Britney; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Escobomb (5:18). Unlisted bout: MaK (led by Jorgy) pinned Christian Atkinson (“The Ak-Attack”, led by Lyndee Atkinson; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Senton Bomb (7:11).

name: GIWF Suicide — 3 Apr 1999

matches.note: Both teams’ debut: Misled Youth (billed Flammable and Freak) beat the Mighty Israelites (Shylock and “The Mighty One” Solomon) when Flammable’s tiger driver pinned Shylock in the back of the arena (15:18). Flammable has no iwf/giwf/uwf record.
Krozor’s GIWF debut: both men were counted out brawling outside (a double countout).

The Grim Reaper was counted out after a masked man attacked him at ringside and unmasked as his Elemental Warriors stablemate John Constantine; Akira and the Sandman appeared beside Constantine in smoke; Al Crud won (8:09).
For the GIWF Television Title (the page prints no match header): Studog Escobar, with G-Lite and John Barnes at ringside, beat the champion Ozzy Douglas with the Escobomb and won the title (8:04).
For the GIWF World Tag-Team Championships: the champions the Dreamwarriors (led by Slaine) kept the titles when Jack of AmWt submitted to Sandman’s Dreamweaver (7:41).

notes: Unlisted bout: The Golden Drifter (with Sexy Torquay) beat The Assassin (“Big Ed, The Ruthless Bastard”, led by Britney; no iwf/giwf/uwf record), who had attacked before the bell: a second Badger Finisher got the pin (6:34).

name: GIWF Suicide — 17 Apr 1999

matches.note: The Dark Lords (Evil and Gabrielle, Gabrielle returning; Luca and Icartai with them) against the TV champion Studog Escobar and G-Lite Maxout (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), led by John Barnes: Gabrielle shut John Barnes in a casket and threw Studog into another, the Mighty Israelites (Shylock and Solomon) attacked Gabrielle and the bell rang; the Dark Lords were given the win (8:55).

matches.stipulation: Four Corners match for the TV Title
matches.note: For the GIWF World Television Title, The Golden Drifter the special referee: Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) and the Grim Reaper were both counted out brawling outside after Akira grabbed Spectre from behind; Al Crud and the champion Studog Escobar then pinned each other with Crud’s bridging back suplex — a draw, and Studog kept the title (12:02).
For the GIWF North American Championship: Akira won when the champion Peter Steele was disqualified for refusing to break a chokehold (7:28).

notes: Unlisted bout: Krozor attacked before the bell and pinned Daemon (formerly Angel of Death; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Super-Tombstone (5:08).

matches.note: E Razor beat Krozor (5:12).
The Golden Drifter beat “The General” Mike Sandman, led by Dawn (5:33).

name: GIWF Suicide — 15 May 1999

matches.note: Misled Youth (Freak and Jack Manson; Jack Manson has no iwf/giwf/uwf record) against the Dreamwarriors: the ten-minute time limit expired.

A triangle match with the debuting Ice J (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), whom Pyro, Freak and Jack Manson had attacked in his dressing room: Pyro pinned Krozor with the Inferno, then Ice J pinned Pyro with the Ice Breaker Powerbomb and won (7:43).

notes: Unlisted bout: tag team match The Dark Lords (Evil and Gabrielle) beat Gangster Power (billed “Ganster Power”: Franky Devlan and Nails Zanetti, led by “Chicago” Mike; no iwf/giwf/uwf record): Evil pinned Nails Zanetti with the Damnation (5:39), and the pair then hung Gangster Power from crucifixes.

name: GIWF Suicide — 22 May 1999

matches.note: The Phenomenons, led by Borrico Agujero, The Punisher and “Suave” Stevie West, beat Henrique Escobar and John Barnes; Shane Stone pinned Barnes with the Cyclone (6:19).

notes: Unlisted bout: The Grim Reaper beat “Coldfire” Zach Shook (no GIWF record) (2:04).

matches.note: Tag match: the Swinging Hipsters (Mike Powers and Austin Myers, led by Miss Piccadilly) against the Cossack Warriors (Ivan and Yuri Kickabollockov, led by “The Mad Monk” Rasputin; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Ivan Kickabollockov pinned Mike Powers after the Vodka Flame Breath; the Cossack Warriors won (7:18).

Tag match: the Dark Lords (Evil and “The Fallen Angel” Gabrielle, with Luca at ringside working a winch) against the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero, The Punisher and “Suave” Stevie West). Lew Spectre, kidnapped by Evil at Tuesday Night Global, was lowered from the ceiling; Curt Raines ran in with a sledgehammer and a crowbar, knocked Luca off the winch and threw the sledgehammer to Stone, who hit Evil with it — the referee called for the bell and the Dark Lords were given the match (4:00). Stone, Cameron, Raines and the freed Spectre then laid out the Dark Lords, Hector and the Acolytes; Spectre destroyed the casket with the sledgehammer.

For the GIWF Intercontinental Title: the double champion Cockney Rebel against Studog Escobar (led by John Barnes). Studog won the title with the Esco ‘nuclear’ bomb (13:39). The Youngbloods then attacked: Curt Raines, Lew Spectre and Shane Stone came to the ring, and the referee — who had levelled the Rebel with a chair — unmasked as Eric Cameron; they beat down the Rebel and Hamish McGrubber (Raines drove the sledgehammer into McGrubber’s knee), Stone and Cameron gave the Rebel the Phenomenal Ending, and Al Crud and Pete Steele made the save.

Tag match: Misled Youth (Freak and Jack Manson; Jack Manson has no iwf/giwf/uwf record) against Gangster Power (Nails Zanetti and a masked man standing in for the injured Franky, led by “Chicago” Mike; Gangster Power and Nails Zanetti have no record). The Masked Man hit Jack Manson with the Guillotine Finisher and unmasked as David Rico (“I WAS DEAD, BUT I HAVE RISEN”), with Evil watching from the ramp; Freak dragged Manson out and the two escaped through the crowd. No result was given.

The decider of the 1999 Stable Wars (the final had ended with Curt Raines and Pete Steele pinning each other), with Coma — Commissioner Rosso’s wrestling persona — as special guest referee: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) for the Youngbloods against Al Crud (with the Mitchell Brothers and The Guv’nor) for the Clash; the prize a shot at the titles of the winner’s choice. Coma ejected Vaughn, the Guv’nor and the Mitchell Brothers; Crud submitted to the Figure-Four Sleeper (14:18) and the Youngbloods became the 1999 GIWF Stable Wars champions.

Tag match: the Dark Lords (Evil and “The Fallen Angel” Gabrielle) against the debuting team of the Grim Reaper and Darkside. Gabrielle pinned the Grim Reaper after the Fall from Grace; the Dark Lords won (5:39). Gabrielle then helped the Reaper to his feet.

For the GIWF Television Title: Pyro (champion, his first defence) against “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn). Pyro took the brawl outside and Spectre was counted out (6:12); the commentators called Pyro “only the third man to ever beat Lew Spectre”.

Main event, a non-title ladder match: the GIWF World Heavyweight Champion Hamish McGrubber against “Bobby Brian Bangemhard” the Bum Boozler (led by Gimp), for the key to the chastity belt the Clash had locked on the Boozler, hung above the ring. The Boozler climbed the ladder and retrieved the key (15:32).

Opening match, refereed by Steven Lodge: “Superstar” Ace Thunder (led by Kitten) against Ice J, a feud Ace declared over. Kitten distracted the referee and Ice J; Ace hit Ice J with her stiletto heel and pinned him (4:19).

Cage tag match: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero) against the Cossack Warriors (Ivan and Yuri Kickabollockov, led by Rasputin; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Yuri pinned Cameron after the Cossack Kick Frenzy on an “unbelievably fast” count — the referee, Keith Burge, unmasked as Alexi, who announced he would train the Cossacks and taunted Cameron. The Cossack Warriors won (6:37).

Main event for the GIWF Television Title, refereed by Steven Lodge: Pyro (champion) against “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn), the second week running. Pyro submitted to the Figure-Four Sleeper (10:00) and Lew Spectre won the TV Title, the first piece of gold he had held in the GIWF.

Tag match: the Dreamwarriors (Sandman and John Constantine) against RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ), in RIMJOB’s GIWF wrestling debut. Sandman caught Triple J in the Dreamweaver and the referee stopped the match; the Dreamwarriors won (7:13).

For the GIWF Television Title: the champion “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against “The Executioner” David Rico (led by David Head). Two masked men came to the ring and struck Rico with a skull staff; the referee called for the bell and Rico was given the match (5:34) — Spectre kept the title. Misled Youth (Pyro, Ace Thunder, the Iron Priest, Jack Manson and Freak) then ambushed Spectre and dragged him under the ring, and the Youngbloods went under after them.

For the GIWF North American Title: the champion Cockney Rebel against a masked mystery opponent — replaced when the Bum Boozler assaulted the masked man backstage and took his place (led by Gimp). The Rebel was counted out and the Boozler given the match (12:47). Lew Spectre then modelled the North American belt; he, Richard Ray Vaughn and the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, with Borrico Agujero) laid out the Rebel and the Mitchell Brothers — Spectre and Stone powerbombed the Rebel through three tables and Cameron dived onto the wreckage — while the Boozler attacked Hamish McGrubber.

Tag match: the Grim Reaper and Darkside against Misled Youth (Freak and Jack Manson). John Constantine distracted the referee and Akira hit Darkside with a baseball bat; Freak pinned Darkside with the shooting star press and Misled Youth won (6:17).

For the GIWF Television Title: the champion “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against “The Executioner” David Rico (led by David Head) — scheduled as a three-way decider after Highland Games, cut to one on one after Spectre, Stone and Cameron locked Studog Escobar in the boot of a car and drove off with him. Rico pinned Spectre with the Execution and won the title (7:26). The two masked men then attacked Rico and were revealed as his own stable-mates: the Grim Reaper broke the skull staff over him and spike-piledrove him onto a chair.

name: GIWF Suicide — 10 Jul 1999
notes: Unlisted bout: Kevin Skinz (led by Mrs. Betty Skinz) against “The Trainer” Alexi (no iwf/giwf/uwf record): the recovered page ends mid-match and the result is lost.

matches.note: Tag match, a sequel to Global Warming (the Israelites’ golf buggy ran over Eric Cameron in the chase for the Diamond Ducat of Dorking): the Mighty Israelites (Solomon and Shylock) against the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero, with Bob the Robot at ringside). Cameron whipped Solomon into Bob the Robot outside and Solomon was counted out; the Phenomenons won (6:40), their third win in a row.

I Quit match to settle the GIWF’s best submission wrestler: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against “The Brooklyn Basher” E Razor. Razor never said “I quit”: caught in Spectre’s double chickenwing, he failed the arm-drop check and the referee stopped the match; Lew Spectre won (11:50).

For the GIWF Television Title, a 2-on-1 handicap match booked by Commissioner Rosso as punishment: the champion “Superstar” Ace Thunder against RIMJOB (J. Harold Christ and Triple J). Twiztid hit the ring and struck Ace with a chair; the referee called for the bell and Ace kept the title by disqualification (5:52) — not the clean win the “Shadow” demanded for Kitten’s return.

First round of the GIWF Tag-Team Titles tournament, refereed by Nelson Steel: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero, with Bob the Robot) against the Golden Drifter and Big Mac Guyver (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Deke Aurora and Nephilim came through the crowd and made off with the Phenomenons’ “Universal Tag Straps”; Shane Stone pinned the Golden Drifter with the Cyclone (5:20).

Non-title match, refereed by Dermott Gallagher: the GIWF North American Champion Cockney Rebel against the newcomer El Leon (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). The Rebel attacked before the bell and threw El Leon out of the ring, where he was counted out; the Cockney Rebel won (7:28). A masked man helped El Leon to his feet.

Last first-round bout of the GIWF World Tag Team Title tournament: Team Esco (“110%” Henrique Escobar and “The Greatest Footballer Alive” John Barnes), the longest-reigning tag champions, against RIMJOB (J. Harold Christ and Triple J). Triple J pinned John Barnes after the Tombstone; RIMJOB won (18:44) and went into the battle royal.

For the GIWF Television Championship, billed as an “I Quit” match with managers barred from ringside: the champion “The Brooklyn Basher” E Razor against “The Fallen One” Nephilim. E Razor tapped and Nephilim won the title (9:39); the Masked Man and El Leon carried off Nephilim’s manager Angelique and Nephilim chased after them.

Tag match, the Fomorians’ debut: the Asylum (Black Dragon and Darkside) against the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey). Underground came to the ring; Eriu and Tethra hit Black Dragon with the Kissing the Blarney Stone and Eriu pinned him (8:25). Underground then tied up the Fomorians to pour sewage over them, and the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron) ran in with chairs, poured the sewage over Abdul Rahaman and fled laughing.

Quarter-final battle royal of the GIWF World Tag Team Title tournament (over the top, both feet on the floor), with Lew Spectre on commentary: RIMJOB (J. Harold Christ and Triple J), the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero), the Brotherhood (Phoenix and Raven), Misled Youth (Freak and “Mad” Jack Manson) and Underground (Da Heat and Abdul Rahaman, led by Carl Big). Cameron was eliminated; Stone, thrown over by Da Heat, touched the floor with only one foot, flipped back in while Cameron pulled down the top rope, and clotheslined Da Heat out — the Phenomenons won (20:44) and went straight to the final at Redemption.

For the GIWF Intercontinental Championship, a triangle match with the interim Commissioner Lew Spectre as referee: “Unforgiven” Ben Jackson, David Rico (led by David Head) and the champion Cpl. Punishment (led by Richard Ray Vaughn). Spectre provoked Rico into hitting him and disqualified him; Spectre and the Corporal then beat down Ben Jackson (a bulldog off the top, the Figure Four Sleeper, a double powerbomb through two chairs, the Lethal Injection and a bat to the ribs) while the Phenomenons brawled with Deke Aurora and Nephilim. The fed’s verdict: “The winner is No Contest.” (17:47); Cpl. Punishment kept the title.

“Rocky Challenge” for the GIWF North American Championship, managers banned from ringside: the champion Cockney Rebel against “The Stylemeister” Lyle Wile. As the Rebel hit Wile with the Last Orders the Phenomenons ran in; Lew Spectre low-blowed the Rebel and Shane Stone hit him with a chair, and the referee called for the bell — the Rebel won by disqualification (18:40). Spectre, Stone and Cameron then powerbombed him through tables, Cameron hit a Stardust Press through three tables of chairs, thumbtacks and trashcans, and Spectre and Stone finished him with the Legend Killer.

Main event, a Portree Strap match (“Lew Spectre’s Version”: touch all four turnbuckles in a row, barbed wire for ropes, taped fists, a fire extinguisher on a pole): Al Crud against “The Highlander” Hamish McGrubber, who announced before the bell that he was leaving the GIWF for a new British federation. The time limit expired and the match went on; McGrubber placed Crud on all four turnbuckles and won (37:51).

North American Tag Team tournament match: North/South Express (Josh Dillinger — spelt “Dillenger” in the match text — and Titan) against “The Fallen One” Nephilim and “The Canadian Luchadore” Deke Aurora (led by Angelique). Shane Stone and Eric Cameron walked down with a baseball bat and balls, stopped the match to play baseball, and Cameron hit Dillinger with the bat; the referee called for the bell and the Express won by disqualification (5:13), a result the commentators credit to the Phenomenons.

North American Tag Team tournament match: the former champions Team Esco (“110%” Henrique Escobar and John Barnes) against RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ). Thanatos appeared on the Global-tron holding Ahmed; John Barnes released his hold and shouted “I Quit”. RIMJOB won (7:13).

“Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against the Masked Man (led by Speaker), the man who had been haunting him. They brawled outside the ring, Vaughn’s interference going both ways, and both were counted out: the verdict was a double countout.

The Rico brothers’ grudge match: the GIWF World Champion “The Executioner” David Rico (led by David Head) against Guy Rico (led by Luca) and Marc Rico (neither has an iwf/giwf/uwf record). David Rico pinned Guy after the Execution (7:25). As the brothers reunited, Lew Spectre, Shane Stone, Eric Cameron and Corporal Punishment laid all three out; Spectre wrecked David Rico’s knee.

For the GIWF Television Title: the champion “The Stylemeister” Lyle Wile against “Unseen” White Wolf. While Sarah distracted the referee Ben Jackson hit Wile with the Unforgiven DDT; White Wolf pinned him after the Artic Splash and won the title (6:38).

North American Tag Team tournament semi-final: the Fan-Tastics (Stalker and Obsessed, led by Hyper Girl) against the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey). Tethra and Obsessed fought on the floor and both teams were counted out on what the commentators called a fast count by Toby Jenkins: the verdict was a double countout, which put Tropical Storm through to the final.

North American Tag Team tournament semi-final: RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ) against North/South Express (Titan and Josh Dillinger, spelt “Dillenger” in the match text). Dillinger’s Lone Star Press hit his own partner when J. Harold Christ slipped Titan’s hold; Christ pinned Dillinger and RIMJOB won (5:23). Dillinger then attacked Titan and told him the team was finished.

Opening match, refereed by Mike Reed: “Unseen” White Wolf against Angel (“From Rio de Janeiro, Brazil… 300 pounds”). They brawled outside the ring and were both counted out: the verdict was a double countout.

Mr. Meaner (Ezra Kazee, whose registry akas include “Mr. Meaner”) against “Ultimate Wrecking Machine” Sebastian Lopez (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), refereed by Graham Poll. Lopez pinned Meaner after the Escape from Judgment (6:01).

Tag match, refereed by Paul Alcock: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero) against RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ). The Phenomenons came out on crutches, in casts and a wheelchair claiming a locker-room assault, then threw off the casts and laid RIMJOB out on the ramp; J. Harold Christ was hurt and “Triple J and Eddie elect to continue”. Deke Aurora and Nephilim came to claim the belts the Phenomenons had taken; Nephilim, in a referee’s shirt, replaced the referee, laid out Stone and counted the pin for Triple J on Eric Cameron. RIMJOB won (10:34).

Main event, billed as Ace Thunder (the GIWF North American Champion, with Kitten) against “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn). Spectre refused to wrestle and named Corporal Punishment in his place. Kitten’s stiletto and Ace’s Thunderclap and Thundershock left Cpl. Punishment motionless, but Ace did not go for a pin; the Order of the Hammer came out from under the ring, the Youngbloods (Lew Spectre, Shane Stone, Eric Cameron, with Lyle Wile) attacked, and no result was given.
Tag match: RIMJOB (Triple J and J. Harold Christ) against the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey). Triple J pinned Eriu after the Tombstone; RIMJOB won (7:23).

For the North American Tag-Team titles: the champions Tropical Storm (Miguel Lanza and Jaime Dermont, billed “Jamie Dermott” in the match text) against the Fan-Tastics (Stalker and Obsessed, led by Hyper Girl). Lanza pinned Stalker after the Reef Dive Driver; Tropical Storm retained (12:20).

For the GIWF Television Title, Deke Aurora’s first defence: the champion “The Canadian Luchadore” Deke Aurora against “The Ultimate Wrecking Machine” Sebastian Lopez (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Aurora pinned Lopez after the Aurora Borealis (8:48).
The Grim Reaper was disqualified for repeated chokeholds; Shark won (9:42). Three masked men then confronted Shark.

For the GIWF Television Title, not elimination rules: as the champion Tremor pinned Angel, Angel rolled him into a reverse cradle and both were pinned (14:03); the title went to the championship committee. Mr. Meaner is Ezra Kazee (registry aka).

For the GIWF Intercontinental Championship: Cpl. Punishment took the first fall (1:12), Ben Jackson the second (12:25); in the third the Knightmare Brigade took out the referee, Mark McCord and then the Youngbloods charged in, and the show went off the air with no result.

Hardcore rules, non-title: the debuting “Hazard” Brian King (led by Shirley Peters) against GIWF Intercontinental Champion Ben Jackson, with Ace Thunder as special guest referee. Thunder DDT’d Hazard, left the ring, and finally hit the Thunderclap on both men, pinned them both himself and was announced the winner (13:00). No decision for either wrestler.

First round of the GIWF Television Title tournament, refereed by Earl Hebner: “Hazard” Brian King (led by Shirley Peters) beat “The Shotgun” Cid Dragon of the Neutralizers (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) (3:18).

First round of the GIWF Television Title tournament, refereed by Danny Davis: Mr. Meaner (Ezra Kazee, whose registry akas include “Mr. Meaner”) against “The Great Neutralizer” Scorpion (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). With the referee down, Devils Disciple tombstoned Scorpion and dragged Meaner on top; Meaner won (5:31) and Devils Disciple recruited him to “The Legacy”.

Tag match, refereed by Mike Reed: the Legacy (Mr. Meaner, on his return from a neck injury, and Angel) against “the Northern Star” Stuart Price (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) and Gurgles (led by Jonny Polo and Lady Luck). Gurgles pinned Angel after the Big Top; Stu Price and Gurgles won (10:27). Mike Sandman then choked Price out with the Dream Time.

Tag match, refereed by Graham Poll: the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey) against the Violent New Breed (Lojack and Devin Ryan). No result: Fey taunted Lojack with a Furby until he snapped, carried her and the Furby out of the ring and the VNB fled with the Fomorians in pursuit (“it looks like this match is off”).

Refereed by Uriah Rennie: Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against Studog Escobar. With the referee down, Cpl. Punishment took the chair Spectre swung and a “cloaked figure” hit Studog; Studog escaped the Figure-Four Sleeper with a modified Escobomb that sent Spectre out of the ring, and Spectre was counted out (14:55). Spectre attacked Studog with a chair after the bell.

Refereed by Graham Poll: Killer Dude beat Angel with a heart punch and the pin (9:14); Angel was left struggling to breathe and the Dude walked off with the Television Title belt Angel had brought to the ring.

For the GIWF North American Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Mike Reed: the champions the Phenomenons (led by Borrico Agujero) against the Dragoons. When Eiji Kanatsu’s plancha landed on Vejiga de Billis, Shane Stone and Eric Cameron carried the injured mule up the ramp and were counted out; the Dragoons won the match (8:35) but the titles, by countout, stayed with the Phenomenons.

For the GIWF Television Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: the new champion “The Psychotic Clown” Gurgles (led by Lady Luck) against Suneil Sangha. Ronny Ramirez knocked out the referee and both men with a barbed-wire baseball bat, laid Gurgles’ arm across Sangha and revived the referee; Gurgles retained (12:51).

Main event tag match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Youngbloods (“The Stylemeister” Lyle Wile and “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre, led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey). No result: a blue mist filled the arena, the lights went out and when they returned Wile and Spectre lay unconscious; the referee called for the bell.
Guitar Ladder match, the March Maelstrom feud continued: the Firestarter, now led to the ring by Hardcore Oddy’s former manager Jess, beat Hardcore Oddy (14:24).

Six man tag, refereed by Nelson Steel: Generation Genesis (Ronny Ramirez and Rage) with the Prodigy (led by Jennifer and Miss Pain) against the former Knightmare Brigade members Suicidal Youth (Ben Jackson and Tremor) with “The One” Neo (no iwf/giwf/uwf record; neither team has a record). Ben Jackson crushed Ramirez’s leg between the ring steps and Ramirez was counted out; Suicidal Youth and Neo won (13:14).

For the GIWF North American Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Graham Poll: the champions the Phenomenons (led by Borrico Agujero) against the Fomorians (Tethra and Eriu, led by Fey), the two longest-reigning teams in GIWF history. Shane Stone pinned Eriu with the Cyclone; the Phenomenons retained (14:35).

Refereed by Graham Poll: Suneil Sangha beat the debuting Phil Anselmo (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when the referee stopped the match on his Canadian Death Lock (7:06). Mid-match the German group (the commentators’ “Nazi’s”) interrupted with a speech about the war between the Youngbloods and the Order and Law & Order.

Tag match, refereed by Mike Reed: the “New” Youngbloods, Lew Spectre and Lyle Wile (the World Tag Team Champions, led to the ring by Richard Ray Vaughn), beat the Violent New Breed (VNB: Lojack and Devin Ryan) when Lew Spectre’s Figure-Four Sleeper made Lojack submit (9:22). The header does not bill it as a title match. Afterwards Lew Spectre and Lyle Wile were found covered head to toe in a red liquid as the Shark’s logo flashed on the screen.
Mike Sandman, led by Dawn, and “Armageddon” Gary Clarke fought to a double countout.
Bahamut pinned Justin Arnold with the Dragon Bomb (10:12).
Suneil Sangha made “The Blade” Stee submit to the Canadian Death Lock (11:05).

No verdict: a hooded man dropped from the rafters on a cable, hanged Lew Spectre by a belt and gave the referee the Lethal Injection; he unmasked as Corporal Punishment, and with Studog Escobar and Pogo (Law & Order) beat Spectre down with a bell, a barbed-wire pogo stick, a cattle prod and a chair.

name: GIWF Suicide — 25 Jun 2000

matches.note: The Vallhallans, led by Sophia, beat Suicidal Youth (Ben Jackson and Tremor; the team has no GIWF record): Vespasien pinned Tremor with the Valor’s End (10:22).

For the Intercontinental Title number-one contendership, the Youngbloods and the Order banned from ringside: after 53:02 of brawling through the arena Deke Aurora and Lyle Wile clashed heads and were both counted out on the canvas — a double knockout (SCHEMA maps it to “no-contest”).

For the GIWF North American Tag-Team Titles: the Bringers of Darkness, led by The Watcher, beat the champions when Venom made Eiji Kanatsu submit to the Venom Web (25:36). Before the bell the Dark Lords (Gabriel, Evil and Luca) returned.

notes: Unlisted bout: White Wolf beat the debuting “E-Z Punk” Johnny Bravo (no GIWF record) with the Artic Splash (6:37). Unlisted bout: The Judge beat the debuting Cypher (no GIWF record) with the Final Verdict (8:00). Unlisted bout: Announced as a no-disqualification grudge match: B-Z (billed “BZ”; no GIWF record) beat Pogo with the Choke Slam (12:13).

matches.note: “Naitch” Taff (led by Zeta; Thirteen under a new name) against Slasher, the winner to face Gurgles for the THC Title. Taff attacked before the bell; Slasher won by pinfall (11:21). White Wolf attacked Slasher after the match.
“The Bastard” Al Crud against Fagen (led by Sadie), with the Phenomenons on commentary; Al Crud won by pinfall (18:50).

Tag match, refereed by Mike Reed: the Irish Hood (Cluney C. and Jack Blarney) beat Great American Youth (Josh and Lance Robbins; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when Jack Blarney pinned Lance Robbins after the Hit da Streets (5:19).

For the GIWF North American Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Mike Reed: the Bringers of Darkness (c) (Venom and Onslaught, led by the Watcher) beat the Phenomenons, Shane Stone and Eric Cameron (the tag-team commissioners, led by Borrico Agujero), and kept the titles. With the Watcher distracting the referee, Killer Dude drove his golf club between Eric Cameron’s legs and gave both Phenomenons the Killer Smash, and Venom made the pin (19:08).

matches.stipulation: Television Title match — two out of three falls
matches.note: Christian Goodwill, the Television Champion, against Inferno (Jay Phoenix's masked GIWF billing), two out of three falls, refereed by Nelson Steel. Inferno took the first fall with an inside cradle (3:22) and Goodwill the second with the Sin Slam (19:20). In the third, with Inferno covering Goodwill after the Meltdown, the lights went out and Slasher struck both men with a flaming chair, threw Inferno from the ring and drove Goodwill through a burning, glass-strewn table. No decision was announced; the commentary guessed that Goodwill kept the title.

Both men's debut: "The Man" Lee Coulter against Lucas Hardy (no GIWF record), with a pair of Coulter's sunglasses hung above the ring; the first man to climb a ladder and pull them down won. Lee Coulter retrieved his sunglasses (8:26).

For the GIWF Television Title, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the champion Ezra Kazee against "Rock Hot" Joe Kenney, led by Chani. Joe Kenney pinned Kazee after the Rock Hot Drop (7:47) and became the new Television Champion; Kazee shook his hand afterwards.

Main event, tag match refereed by Mike Reed: the Youngbloods' World Champion Lew Spectre and North American Champion Deke Aurora, led by Richard Ray Vaughn, against Gurgles and Inferno, led by Lady Luck. Vaughn's briefcase shot meant for Gurgles hit Spectre instead; the time limit expired and the referee let the match continue; Inferno pinned Deke Aurora with the Meltdown (25:16) for a clean win over the two champions.

Refereed by Nelson Steel: "Maury" Maurice against "Main Event" Eric Cameron, led by Borrico Agujero. If Maurice won, Pete the PG Tips Monkey, held in Eric Cameron's "de-programming scheme", would be returned to partner him against the Dragoons at Northern Lights. Borrico Agujero twice hit Maurice with the Mexican Cane, and Eric Cameron pinned him with the Showstopper (12:27), keeping Pete with the Phenomenal Clique.

Refereed by Nelson Steel; billed as Inferno, three days before his North American Title match with Deke Aurora, Aurora's career on the line, at Northern Lights. Inferno pinned Ben Jackson ("Unforgiven", filed under ben-jericho) with the Meltdown (6:27).

Main event, a handicap bout: Lady Luck and her mystery partner, Miss Tress (no GIWF record), against Lew Spectre, whose partner Lyle Wile had walked out on the Youngbloods at the top of the show. Gurgles sat at ringside and Apocalypse accompanied Miss Tress. Lady Luck and Miss Tress hit Spectre with a double low blow and pinned him with a double inside cradle; Spectre complained of a fast count. Afterwards Spectre attacked both women and put Lady Luck in the Figure Four Sleeper until Gurgles broke it with his crutch; Gary Clark, Inferno and White Wolf came through the crowd and joined Gurgles and Lady Luck in beating Spectre down, Inferno with the Meltdown, and Lady Luck finished him with the Happy Hammer.
Refereed by Graham Poll, in both men's first GIWF appearance: "Superstar" Johnny Walker pinned Olaf (no GIWF record) with the Heartbreaker (14:15).

Tag match, refereed by Graham Poll: the Hooded Perverts (Tommo and Ched, led by Dirty Dave) beat Apocalypse (Richard Gordon and Steven Fredericks; no GIWF record) when Richard Gordon submitted to Tommo's Stained Trousers (15:40).

The Television Champion Lee Coulter ("The Man", led by Trin) against the debuting Ethan (no GIWF record), the title belt hung above the ring. Ethan hit Coulter with a sledgehammer, but "Rock Hot" Joe Kenney came out and knocked Ethan off the ladder as he reached for the belt; Coulter retrieved the belt and retained (19:01).

Main event, refereed by Nelson Steel: Cpl Punishment, Jay Phoenix, the new World Champion Gurgles (led by Lady Luck) and Lyle Wile, on the first card after Northern Lights, where Inferno stood revealed as Jay Phoenix and won the North American Title (which he renamed the Native American Title). Lew Spectre came to ringside and hit Jay Phoenix with a chair as he hit the ropes. The time limit expired and the referee let the match continue; Jay Phoenix pinned Gurgles with the Meltdown (23:49), and Gurgles complained about a fast count. Afterwards Luca fired a weighted net from L.U.C.A.B.O.T over all four men, nailed it to the canvas and challenged Jay Phoenix for a title shot.
Refereed by Nelson Steel: the debuting “Mark Simon” Ca$h beat “Matthew Goulding” Ermac (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Paydirt (8:28).
Refereed by Graham Poll: Snake Phoenix beat The Ripper (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Whiplash (5:18). Snake Phoenix is not Jay Phoenix (the commentary: “no relation to Jay”).
Refereed by Nelson Steel: Tequilla (led by Rosita) and Davey Boy Spliff (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) brawled outside and were both counted out.
Refereed by Graham Poll: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led to the ring by Richard Ray Vaughn) beat Scott Ross (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when the Figure-Four Sleeper made him submit (16:34).

Billed “The Icon -v- Lee Coulter”: “The Icon” is Mike Platinum, defending the GIWF TV Title by the commentary, led to the ring by Agent Jimmy Gold; “The Man” Lee Coulter was led by Trin. Trin climbed on the apron with her ringing mobile phone and handed it to Lee Coulter, and while he took the call Mike Platinum dove over the top rope and drove him through a table (12:23).
Refereed by Uriah Rennie: CA$H ("Mark Simon") pinned "Munch Munch" Chomps after a low blow (11:19).

The Serial Thrillers' debut (Adrian Devlin and Gabriel Talbot, managed by "Dangerous" Donovan Lane) against the Phenomenons, Commissioners of the Tag Team Division, led by Borrico Agujero; refereed by Uriah Rennie. Shane Stone faked an injury to the leg in his cast and sprayed silly string in Devlin's face; Devlin swung at Eric Cameron and knocked the referee out, Cameron decked him with the steel cane, and the Phenomenons hit Gabriel Talbot with the Phenomenal Ending, smashed carved pumpkins over both men's heads and left them in the corner with a 'Happy Halloween' sign. No decision was given.

Refereed by Graham Poll: the Native American (North American) Champion Jay Phoenix against the debuting Alex Smith (no GIWF record), led by Ole Jim; the commentators called it Alex Smith's shot at the champion in his debut. Ole Jim distracted Phoenix at ringside; Jay Phoenix pinned Alex Smith after a low blow (15:12).

name: GIWF Suicide — 12 Nov 2000
notes: Unlisted bout: Against Krushing Time (Krush and Maximus; no GIWF record). No result: as Adrian Devlin covered Krush after the Scream Machine, Chomps ran in, laid out the referee and put Krush and Maximus through a chair and a barbed-wire table, and he and the Serial Thrillers left them bleeding.

matches.note: Refereed by Graham Poll: the debuting “Superstar” Johnny Walker and Eclipse (no iwf/giwf/uwf record; the uwf’s Shawn Eclipse is another record, not this man) brawled outside and were both counted out.

Tag match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Too Smutty (the Muff master and Silicone Trish) lost to Fat & Small (Chris Hurst and Davo; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when Davo pinned Silicone Trish after the Main Course (8:04).

Billed “Rock Hot -v- Eric Cameron & [Shane Stone]”, refereed by Graham Poll: Rock Hot wrestled as “The Blood-Rush Counterfeit” Joe Kenny (led by Chani) and pinned “Main Event” Eric Cameron (led by Borrico Agujero) with the Rock Hot Drop (11:25). Shane Stone came out for the second leg, but it never began: the Serial Thrillers (Devlin and Talbot) ran in and drove Rock Hot through a table with the Adrenalin Rush, and the half ended with the Phenomenons standing awestruck.

Main event, refereed by Nelson Steel: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against “The Supreme Master of Controversy” Hybrid (Adam Finn). With both men brawling at ringside, Jay Phoenix ran in and hit both of them with a moonsault off the top turnbuckle, and neither beat the count — a double countout.

For the GIWF Television Championship, refereed by Graham Poll: Lee Coulter (c), led to the ring by Joe Kenny, Trin, Dirty Dave and Chani, retained against “Blondie” Craig Wright, led by Linzi, pinning him with the End of the Line (spelled “Eng Of The Line” on the card) after Joe Kenny had hit Wright with the Cricket Bat (13:44).

Main event, a triangle match refereed by Stephen Lodge; Lew Spectre was led to the ring by Richard Ray Vaughn. Jay Phoenix hit Spectre with a chair and chased Adam Finn to the back; a cage holding Jay Phoenix was then lowered from above with a cloaked man standing on it, Hybrid ran back in and hit Spectre with two Exclamation Marks, the Spettro Di Avversione Mafia chased Finn into the crowd, and the referee ruled a no-contest.

name: GIWF Suicide — 3 Dec 2000

matches.note: Made a GIWF World Heavyweight Title match at the bell by Lew Spectre, who came out as the special referee: he fought off the Clique’s double-teams, then stopped his count on Al Crud’s pin at two, hit Crud with a chair and counted Lyle Wile’s pin on him; Wile retained (19:18). The Crimson Ghost (identity not given) attacked Corporal Punishment.

notes: Unlisted bout: Kombat (no GIWF record) beat “Superstar” Johnny Walker, making him submit to the K-Bombed (9:13). Unlisted bout: The Dragoons, back from their lay-off, beat Apocalypse (Richard Gordon and Steven Fredericks, “Decimation” and “Elimination”; no GIWF record) when Eiji Kanatsu (Tiamat) pinned Richard Gordon with the Dragon Dive (11:44), then put both men through tables.

matches.note: Refereed by Uriah Rennie: “Blondie” Craig Wright, led to the ring by Linzi, pinned Draven Lox, led by Claudia, with the Queen (5:33).

Refereed by Stephen Lodge: “Munch Munch” Chomps and “Dangerous” Donovan Lane against Junior Ste (billed “Jnr Ste”; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Junior Ste made Donovan Lane submit to the Hyperextension (11:12). Earlier that night Chomps had set Too Smutty’s car alight with them inside; their scheduled match with The Revolution did not take place.
Refereed by Ian Willis: “The Eternal Flame” Brad Johnson against Enigma, both men in their second GIWF stint; they brawled on the floor until both were counted out.

Main event, billed as Al Crud & Lew Spectre v. Lyle Wile & Cpl Punishment; after the four men brawled, Jae O’Connor re-made it Corporal Punishment & Al Crud v. Lew Spectre & Lyle Wile, refereed by Graham Poll. Teddy “Velvet” Jackson bribed the referee out of the ring and took over; the Don’t Brothers attacked Al Crud, Dave Don’t hit Spectre with a chair, and The Prodigy forced Jackson to count as he dragged Al Crud onto Lew Spectre for the pin: “Winners: Corporal Punishment and Al Crud.”

Tag team match, refereed by Ian Willis: billed “The Revolution” (an aka of the R.P.A.), Skull and Deck against the Hooded Perverts, Ched and Tommo (led to the ring by Dirty Dave). Ched and Tommo beat the count back into the ring and Deck did not: a count-out win for the Hooded Perverts (35:32).

Refereed by Nelson Steel: the debuting “The Attacker in the Dark” Mad Man Max against “Blondie” Craig Wright (led to the ring by Linzi). After Max’s DDT left Wright out cold, Lee Coulter ran in and gave both men the End Of The Line, then wrecked Max’s leg with a steel chair; the verdict was a no contest.
Refereed by Nelson Steel: the returning Christian Goodwill beat Enigma with the Sin Slam (12:53).

Refereed by Nelson Steel: Benito Cavalera (led to the ring by Massimilano Cavalera) and Kombat (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), who had been attacked by Skull and Deck earlier in the show, brawled outside and were both counted out.

Main event, refereed by Stephen Lodge: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against “Prodigal Son” The Prodigy, with Al Crud, Cpl Punishment, Luca, Shane Stone, Gurgles, Hybrid and Lyle Wile as lumberjacks (Celest was taken out on the ramp before the bell by Benito Cavalera, posing as Nephilim). The lumberjacks ended up brawling with each other and the match had no decision.
Refereed by Ian Willis: “Baby Physco” Trent Lucas, in his GIWF debut, beat the debuting Chronic (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Spotlight (7:51).

Refereed by Graham Poll: Slasher and Enigma traded the Slasher Dive and the Serial Killer until Enigma’s lancet-arch left both men’s shoulders on the mat for the three count — “Both combatants have been pinned !”

North American Title tournament, first round, refereed by Ian Willis: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against “LB” L.U.C.A.B.O.T, Luca the Imp in the cockpit. After Lew Spectre collided with the referee, Jay Phoenix ran in with a crowbar, disabled LUCABOT and left, and Lew Spectre made the cover (8:21).

The final of the tournament for the vacant GIWF North American Title (the main event), refereed by Ian Willis: Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) against Al Crud. No decision is given: LUCABOT came to the ring and lassoed both men, Luca the Imp berated them (“WANTED Poo Sphincter!”), LUCABOT beat them down, and Luca declared “If I can’t have the North American Title… then NO ONE can!”; GIWF officials took the belt away.

Opening match, refereed by Isaiah Haywood: The Plague, led to the ring by Evan McCann, beat the debuting “OD” Bert Hummel (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), said to be carrying a chest injury, with the Black Death (7:21).

First round (first bracket) of the tournament for the returning North American Tag-Team Titles, refereed by Nelson Steel: Pretty in the City (“Twice as Nice” Mark McCord, who has no iwf/giwf/uwf record, and “The Beautiful One” Daneel McCord) against the Hardcore Elements. Roadkill Grill pinned Mark McCord with the Roadkill Cafe (11:27).

First round (first bracket) of the North American Tag-Team Title tournament, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Star Motion (Brent Alpine and “The Cutter” Dallas Culture) against the header’s “Mystery Team”, revealed at the introductions as The Bushmen (Bigfoot and Sasquatch, led to the ring by Yeti; no giwf/uwf record). Sasquatch pinned Dallas Culture with the Squash Bomb (9:54).

GIWF World Television Title (“THE Title”, as the champion styled it), refereed by Nelson Steel: “A.S.S.” Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third (c) beat Kombat (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) with the Shake-Spear (2:24).

Main event, tag match refereed by Graham Poll: Pete Steele and Al Crud (led by Ole Gus) against Jay Phoenix and Cpl. Punishment. Luca rode LUCABOT to ringside; LUCABOT threw Jay Phoenix a bow and fired an arrow into the Corporal as he covered Pete Steele; Luca pointed at Jay, Jay threw the bow down, and the referee called for the bell — Al Crud and Peter Steele the winners (17:29). Afterwards LUCABOT shaved Jay Phoenix’s head, and Lew Spectre ran in with a chair and laid out Al Crud and Luca.
“The Supreme Master of Controversy” Hybrid against Craig Wright (led by Linzi); Hybrid won by pinfall with the Exclamation Mark (14:24).

Billed for the GIWF Television Title, but champion Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third declared it a non-title match on his way to the ring; he beat Chomps (11:24), and the commentators said he should be stripped for failing to defend.

Refereed by Isiah Haywood: Ice Cold Killa beat “The Ultimate Fighting Machine” Martial Madman (led to the ring by Miss Tasha Love; no iwf/giwf/uwf record), who had attacked him before the bell, with the Heartbreaker (7:46).

World Heavyweight title match, refereed by Uriah Rennie: the champion Luca, in the L.U.C.A.B.O.T., retained against the Regal Rumble 2001 winner “The Bloody One” Ricky Ketsu-Eki, who submitted to the Pneumatic Nut Crush (19:15).

Hardcore match refereed by Nelson Steel: The Reaper beat Chomps after Max Damage came out with a barbed-wire 2x4, turned on Chomps, helped The Reaper and revived the referee for the three count (8:10); Max Damage then named The Reaper the newest member of Maximum Damage.

Refereed by Uriah Rennie: Benito Cavalera (led by Massimilano Cavalera) lost to RiVeN (Chris Hatchett), Celest’s brother. With the referee following Celest around the ring, The Preacher injected Cavalera at ringside and RiVeN pinned him after the Everlourne Execution and the Dark Omen (18:59).

Main event, a non-title match refereed by Graham Poll: “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn) beat the Intercontinental Champion “Crash” Pete Steele (led by Ole Gus). With Graham Poll knocked out by Ole Gus, Spectre broke Vaughn’s briefcase over Steele, wrecked his knee with two chairs and a top-rope dive, then held the figure four until the revived referee saw Steele’s arm fall three times.
Mike Montgomery lost to “The Prophet” Rev. John Camen (billed Reverend John Camon; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) by pinfall (10:49).
Craig Wright (led by Linzi) attacked Max Damage before the bell and won by pinfall (11:00).
North American Tag Team Title Tournament: the Dragoons (Eiji Kanatsu and Bahamut) beat the Rebel Generation (Snake Phoenix and Max Sin) by pinfall (7:59).
“Dangerous” Donovan Lane, four days into his GIWF Television Title reign, against Ice Cold Killa: a double countout.

Refereed by Uriah Rennie: Mike Montgomery beat “The Prophet” Rev. John Camen (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) in their rematch, pinning him after a low blow (8:22); the Forces of Darkness then laid Camen in a coffin.

North American Tag Team title defence, refereed by Nelson Steel: the champions the Hardcore Elements (Roadkill Grill and Overturned Car) against the RPA (Skull and Deck). Davey Boy Spliff (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) rode in on a BMX and hit Deck, and the referee called for the bell: the RPA were declared the winners (12:51), and the Hooded Perverts, bursting out from under the announce table, still addressed the Elements as the North American Tag Team champions.

Intercontinental title match: Celest beat the champion “Strictly Business” Lew Spectre (led by Richard Ray Vaughn). Spectre made Celest submit to the Figure-Four Sleeper while the referee lay unconscious, but Al Crud ran in, hit Spectre with two Mother Crudders, dragged Celest on top of him and revived the referee for the three count (12:18). The Crimson Ghost then dropped from the rafters and choked Celest out with a cross-face chicken wing.

I Quit match refereed by Nelson Steel: Max Damage against “Blondie” Craig Wright (led to the ring by Linzi). Wright had Damage in an ankle lock when Mike Montgomery came through the crowd and hit Wright with the Hangman’s Joke and a steel chair; Damage accidentally clotheslined the referee, and his Maximum Damage stable ran in (Krush, Maximus, Reaper). Damage locked Wright in the Maximum Damage and Wright submitted: “The winner is: Max Damage” (0:11:10). Afterwards Montgomery attacked Wright again, and Luca in LUCABOT, the Hooded Perverts and the Reverend John Camon turned on Mike Montgomery, I.C.K. and Trent Lucas: the Common Cause was formed.

Tag team match refereed by Graham Poll: the Serial Thrillers (Gabriel Talbot and Adrian Devlin, led to the ring by Tammy Lynn Sytch) beat the rookie team Degenerados los Conquistadors (Hunter and Spazz; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Talbot pinned Spazz after the Stimulator from the turnbuckle (0:09:25).
Non-title cage match: Jared Crafter of the Forces of Darkness against the GIWF World Champion Luca the Imp, who wrestled as L.U.C.A.B.O.T. L.U.C.A.B.O.T. escaped the cage to win (0:10:26).

For the GIWF Television Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: billed as I.C.K. against the champion Pete Steele, but Pete Steele did not appear and Ole Gus came out in his place as “The GIWF Television Champion”. Ice Cold Killa hit the Killa Smash and pinned Ole Gus (0:01:27) — the title history’s “def. Ole Gus (??) — SAS” (reign giwf-television-r061).

GIWF World Tag-Team Title match, refereed by Isiah Haywood: the R.P.A (Skull and Deck) beat the champions, the Wimp & Chimp Connection (Maurice and Petey), Skull pinning Maurice after the Red Elbow (10:19). The New Breed (Donovan Lane, Devlin, Talbot and Jake “The Ace” Spade) then beat the new champions down with baseball bats.

Main event for the GIWF Intercontinental Title, refereed by Uriah Rennie: Jay Phoenix (c) against “Crash” Peter Steele (led by Ole Gus). Luca rode a donkey to the ramp and goaded Pete Steele, who left the ring after him and was counted out — Jay Phoenix the winner (21:14). Celest, at ringside, low-blowed Jay Phoenix at the bell and left with the belt; LUCABOT felled Pete Steele with an anchor.

Opening match, refereed by Isiah Haywood: Cpl. Punishment against the debuting “The Bitch Maker” Castor Johnson (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Johnson passed out in the Lethal Injection and the referee stopped the match (8:58).

Tag match, led to the ring by Dirty Dave: the Hooded Perverts (Tommo and Ched) beat Lethal Injection (Chris Patterson and Szpula; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when Tommo covered Szpula (12:03). The Hardcore Elements joined the commentary table; afterwards the Forces of Darkness and Max Damage, Steph Gray and Krushing Time (unmasked from under druid hoods) set Lethal Injection and Craig Wright alight in caskets.

Main event, for the GIWF Intercontinental Title, refereed by Isiah Haywood: Jay Phoenix (champion; “From Death Valley, Texas”) retained against Slasher. The time limit expired and the referee let the match continue; Jay Phoenix pinned Slasher with the Meltdown (20:49).

Tag match: the Dragoons (Tiamat and Bahamut) beat Lethal Injection (Chris Paterson and Szpula; no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when Tiamat pinned Chris Paterson after the Dragon Dive (3:34). The Dragoons then beat both men down with chairs and put Paterson through two tables.

Main event, the number-one contendership to Luca’s World Heavyweight Title, with the stipulations Luca and Jae O’Connor added: no disqualification, and a lumberjack match with Craig Wright and the Hooded Perverts at ringside. The CEO the Prodigy named Pete Steele the referee and warned the brothers they would be suspended for thirty days if they touched anyone but each other. They pulled their blows; Tommo low-blowed Jay Phoenix, and Pete Steele stamped Celest down on top of the hurt Jay Phoenix and counted three. Luca announced Celest the winner; Steele, Wright, the Perverts and Luca then beat both brothers down. Celest went on to face Luca for the title.

Refereed by Graham Poll: “The Bloody One” Ricky Ketsu-Eki against Benjita Oshima (no iwf/giwf/uwf record; the booth calls him Ben Jackson’s latest Japanese persona). Hybrid came to ringside with a chair and drove it into Oshima’s back to break a reverse gory special; Ketsu-Eki hit a reverse double underhook DDT and the referee counted three. Afterwards Hybrid threw the referee out, Ketsu-Eki tried to unmask Oshima, Jaxx ran in and took Hybrid’s Exclamation Mark, and Celest came down and choke-slammed Ketsu-Eki and Hybrid and laid Oshima out with a lariat.

Refereed by Graham Poll: the North American Champion “The Dart-Break Kid” Gary Clark (non-title) against “The Purple One” Leon Hayze (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), led to the ring by Vincent, who hit Clark with a chair twice and cost Hayze when a third swing hit Hayze instead. Clark won by pinfall with the Retribution (0:14:14).

Refereed by Isiah Heywood: the debut of “the Dolomite” Danny Duran (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) against “Dangerous” Donovan Lane, back from his European tour. Lane won by pinfall with the Danger Zone (0:04:02).

Tag team match refereed by Des Galpin: the Serial Thrillers (Gabriel Talbot and Adrian Devlin) beat Lethal Injection (Szpula and Chris Patterson; no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Devlin pinned Szpula after the Scream Machine (0:07:19).

Billed as Jaxx and a debuting partner against the Elements of Destruction (“TNT” Tommy N Taylor and The Plague, led by Evan McCann), refereed by Jacob Jeremis. Jaxx never came to the ring: his debuting partner (no iwf/giwf/uwf record) wrestled TNT (no record) and The Plague alone. When The Plague brawled with him into the crowd, a fan in a hat clotheslined him — it was Jaxx, who took TNT out with a chair and a sledgehammer, beat The Plague with the hammer and threw him off the entrance ramp. No decision was announced.

Refereed by Isiah Heywood: “The Corporal” Cpl. Punishment, now the Prodigy’s enforcer, against “The Black Angel” Damian Gilchrist (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). The Corporal locked on his Lethal Injection hold and the referee stopped the match when Gilchrist’s arm fell three times (0:09:20).

Celest against “The Psychotic Clown” Gurgles (led by Lady Luck), with Al Crud as special guest referee. Jay Phoenix came to ringside to cheer on Celest and put the boots to Gurgles; Gurgles swung the Happy Hammer at Phoenix, and Crud jumped in front of it and was knocked out. Phoenix moonsaulted Gurgles through a table from the top turnbuckle; Celest revived Crud, hit the Celestial Annihilation, and the groggy Crud counted three (0:03:04).
For the GIWF Intercontinental Title, refereed by Luke Hutton: the champion “LB” Lucabot (Luca the Imp) beat “The Man” Lee Coulter with a low blow and the pin (12:44).

Refereed by Isiah Heywood: “KJ” Kilo Jones beat Keflon (11:23). Krushing Time (Krush and Maximus) came to ringside, a Tarzan-a-gram, a “Crimson Dude” and the Emerald Haunt dropped from the rafters, Maximus knocked the referee out on the ring post, and Kilo, Krush and Maximus beat Keflon down before Kilo made the cover. The Emerald Haunt was Luca the Imp, who then joined Krushing Time’s stable.

Cpl. Punishment’s North American Title on the line, refereed by Jacob Jeremis: Jay Phoenix and his brother Celest against Cpl. Punishment (c). With Celest’s pin under way, Jay Phoenix moonsaulted onto him and brought the title belt down across his head, then helped the Corporal; Punishment’s Lethal Injection put Celest out and Punishment was announced the winner, but he would not release the hold and the referee reversed the decision — Celest and Jay Phoenix the winners by disqualification (23:10); the title cannot change hands on a disqualification, so Punishment kept it. Afterwards Jay and the Corporal powerbombed Celest onto the Internet desk and Jay legdropped him through it; Jay announced he had joined the Prodigy’s stable (the Prodigy, Al Crud, Cpl. Punishment).

Main event, tag match refereed by Graham Poll: the Bringers of Darkness (Venom and Onslaught, led by the Watcher) against “The Psychotic Clown” Gurgles and “The Dart-Break Kid” Gary Clark (led by Lady Luck and Simon Lyons). Luca brought LUCABOT and Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third to the ring; Onslaught chaired Gurgles, Venom and Saunders kicked Gary Clark down, and Luca introduced his third stable, “The Team That Will Win The Wars” (4T3Ws: the Bringers and Saunders). No decision was given.

The Phenomenons against Lyle Wile and his stable's fourth member, revealed at the entrance as Hybrid, against Cpl. Punishment and Jay Phoenix, refereed by Isiah Heywood. Jay Phoenix and Eric Cameron brawled at ringside through the referee's ten-count, “Suave” Stevie West distracting Phoenix, and the verdict was a double count-out; Wile and Hybrid were neither counted out nor beaten. Afterwards Wile, Hybrid, E-Razor and Studog Escobar beat Phoenix down and, with Benjita Kea and Richard Ray Vaughn, revealed themselves as the new Youngbloods; Vaughn hit Phoenix with the Briefcase of Doom.

A “friendly fight” between Elements of Destruction stable-mates, refereed by Graham Poll: Killer Dude against “TNT” Tommy N Taylor (no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Killer Dude won by pinfall with the Killer Smash (0:11:49).

Billed as the R.P.A. (Skull and Deck) against Blade and a mystery partner, refereed by Graham Poll: Blade announced that his partner was himself and wrestled both men alone. After the referee was knocked down, Jaxx came over the guard-rail with two sledgehammers; Blade and Jaxx hammered Skull and Deck, Blade covered Skull, and Jaxx lifted the referee’s arm for the count: “The winner is Blade.” (0:09:27).
Refereed by Uriah Rennie: Masked Mayhem (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), unbeaten in his one previous GIWF match, against “KJ” Kilo Jones. Kilo Jones won by pinfall with the Overdose (0:08:44).

The Dragoons’ North American Tag Team Titles against Q Factor (Max Queue-a-rollox and Link Anchorman, led by the Klue-Tang-Plan and Helix the Phenomenal Lost Boy). Bahamut snarled at Link Anchorman, who fainted; Bahamut covered him for the three count (0:00:05). Eiji Kanatsu is not named in the bout.

For the GIWF World Heavyweight Championship: the champion “Prodigal Son” The Prodigy (his second defence of the day, after the Chris Williams Cup) against the Hall of Famer “The Stylemeister” Lyle Wile. Luca and Gary Clark interrupted with a bowling routine, announced a strike against the Prodigy’s management, and Luca handcuffed Clark to the top rope; the referee ruled that the match could not continue: “the bout is judged to be a No Contest”.

Opening match, refereed by Isiah Heywood: “The Innovator of Pain” Bruce Gordy lost to the debuting “The Dean Of Destruction” Disaster (no iwf/giwf/uwf record): the lights went out, and when they came back Disaster lay on the prone Gordy for the three count (7:10). Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third, who had arranged it believing Blade was in the match, then used a clipboard to claim Blade had broken the Television Title’s defend-on-every-card rule.
Tag match refereed by Uriah Rennie, Corrupt Judgment’s debut: the R.P.A (Skull and Deck) against Corrupt Judgment (The Judge and The Jury). The Judge pinned Deck with the All Rise (12:16).

Refereed by Graham Poll: Chomps against Max Damage, with no decision. Gary Clark (UP YORS) ran down with a baseball bat while Simon Lyons distracted the referee, smashed Max Damage across the knee and laid Chomps out with a shot to the head — “Chomps... Strike One... Max Damage ... Strike Two...” — and no result was announced.

For Trent Lucas’s THC Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: Trent Lucas (c) against “Wonderwall” Stevie Wonder (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), led to the ring by Chyco Wonder. No decision: Gurgles and Lady Luck (UP YORS) came out to break the match up; Lucas and Wonder turned on Gurgles together, then Team M&M (Senor Mime, Muchacho Mime, Lita and Zoompa Doompa) beat both men down and Gurgles left them unconscious with the Happy Hammer. The title did not change hands.

Tag team match refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Phenomenons (Shane Stone and Eric Cameron, led to the ring by Borrico Agujero) against the Forces of Darkness (Jared Crafter and Riggs; Riggs has no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Riggs’s Apocalypse on Eric Cameron got a near-fall; then Luca (UP YORS), pushing a cardboard cut-out of the Dark Lords, had a skip of trifle dropped from the rafters onto the ring, covering both teams and the referee, who slipped out of the ring and called for a no contest.

Main event, tag team match refereed by Uriah Rennie: the Cybernetic Hardcore Luchadores (CHL #2 and CHL #3 in the ring) against the Dragoons (Bahamut and Eiji Kanatsu), billed as the World and North American Tag Team Champions. No decision: the R.P.A. (Skull and Deck), paid by Luca and joined by two Rastafarian helpers, tazered and beat down all four men.

Billed “Garry Maximum -v- Brad Stratus” (non-title, refereed by Uriah Rennie), but Corporal Punishment had ordered Stratus to stand down and took his place: Cpl. Punishment beat Garry Maximum (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), who submitted to the Lethal Injection (7:46). After the bell Studog Escobar joined Punishment in the ring and Brad Stratus came over the rails to beat Maximum with a Singapore cane and a somersault leg-drop through a chair.

Refereed by Uriah Rennie. Taff (Thirteen), dressed as Neil Diamond, came out miming to Neil Diamond records; while Ezra Kazee had Alexander Sebastian Saunders the Third in a sleeper, Taff got into the ring, hit the referee and Kazee with a chair and pulled Saunders on top of Kazee; Zeta revived the referee with a kiss and he counted the pin (9:46). Taff did not wrestle.
THC Title, refereed by Nelson Steel: the champion “LB” Lucabot (Luca the Imp in L.U.C.A.B.O.T.) retained against Chris Cage, who submitted to the Pneumatic Nut Crush (17:37).
Refereed by Graham Poll: Bruce Gordy lost to the debuting Dark Crusader (no iwf/giwf/uwf record), pinned after the Death Knell (8:17).

Tag team match refereed by Isiah Heywood: Corrupt Judgment (the Judge and the Jury) beat the Forces of Darkness (Jared Crafter and Riggs, who holds no iwf/giwf/uwf record) when the Judge pinned Riggs after the All Rise (9:14).
Tag team match refereed by Isiah Heywood: Street Science (Studog Escobar and E Razor) beat the RPA (Skull and Deck) when Deck submitted to E Razor’s Razors Edge (7:24).

name: GIWF Christmas Clash '99

evidence.note: The GIWF's own ceremony transcripts name the Venetian Home Rumble I -- the Phenomenons vs. Al Crud & the joke gimmick Tom the Christmas Tree -- as "fought at Christmas Clash '99," independently corroborated by a later UWF retrospective and a Christmas Clash 2000 preview.
The announce duo's own retrospective monologue recaps the first Venetian Home Rumble as fought at Christmas Clash, Dec 1999, opponent Al Crud plus a dead Christmas tree partner.
A contributor's own match log lists "23/12/99, Christmas Clash PPV, vs Al Crud/Tom the Christmas Tree/Masked Man" -- the exact date this row uses.

notes: GIWF's surrounding December 1999 shows are held (the weekly Global/Suicide cards through November, and the following year's Christmas Clash 2000); this one is not. Surfaced during the Venetian Home Rumble I sourcing hunt, which confirmed no giwf-christmas-clash-99 row exists anywhere in the served corpus.

name: Chris Williams Memorial Cup III

evidence.note: GIWF Global's own build plugs it directly: "currently away competing in the third annual Chris Williams Cup... the Chris Williams Memorial Cup III on Sunday, June 17th, live on Pay Per View, call your local cable operator now."

Five weeks later, the same broadcast recaps "The Prodigy dismantling Benjita Kea at the second annual Chris Williams Memorial Cup" — the fed's own text billing the same-year event inconsistently (III vs. "second annual"), left as the record shows it rather than resolved.
PWW wrestlers cross over for the annual Cup, roughly two months before the June 17 PPV — pre-tournament build.

Gurgles "miserably fails in the Chris Williams Memorial Cup tournament," and Benjita Kea's own World title shot "at the Chris Williams Cup... came up just short" — post-PPV fallout the following week.
Three more GIWF Suicide broadcasts across the same window reference the Cup's own crowd in attendance, then recap Chris Cage's own and Gurgles' own tournament runs after the fact.

Fourteen months later (UWF Defining Moment, 8 Sep 2002), Chris Cage's attack on Sirius is recalled as happening "at the last Chris Williams Memorial Cup, as well as during the last months of the GIWF" — consistent with this being the most recent Cup as of a promotion that itself folded around the same window.

notes: An external interfed tournament — hosted on Jaymes Faulkner's own rpcommunity.com among other homes — never staged on a held GIWF or UWF page of its own, only referenced, promoted, and recapped across surrounding shows (per THE MEMORIAL WAVE 2's own audit of all fifteen held Chris Williams Memorial Cup references, none of which stage the Cup itself).
